Fraudsters will use unexpected phone calls, doorstep conversations, emails and messages to build trust, create urgency and pressure people into sharing personal information or sending money.

More than a quarter (26%) of people surveyed feel uncomfortable questioning someone claiming to represent a public organisation or essential service provider such as a bank, the police, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC), a delivery company or a utility provider.

But criminals will often pretend to be from trusted organisations to trick people into handing over money.

Some £92.4 million was identified as being stolen by criminals through impersonation scams last year, according to UK Finance figures.

Jess Cook, a spokesperson for Take Five to Stop Fraud, said: “Criminals know it can feel uncomfortable to end a conversation abruptly or question someone claiming to represent a trusted organisation.

“They exploit our instinct to be polite to keep us engaged for longer, and every extra minute gives them more opportunity to build trust, create urgency and persuade us to hand over money or personal information.

“The ‘art of impoliteness’ is about giving people permission to put protection before politeness.

“If someone unexpectedly asks for your money or personal information, stop the interaction.

“Hang up, shut the door, or simply say no. Then verify independently using contact details you trust.

“Any genuine organisation won’t mind you taking the time to check it’s really them.”

Take Five to Stop Fraud is led by UK Finance, in partnership with the banking and financial services sector.

The Take Five to Stop Fraud campaign urges people to:

Stop – You have the right to stop and think before parting with your money or information. It could keep you safe.

Challenge – Hang up, shut the door, close the email or simply say “no”. Only criminals will try to rush or panic you.

Protect – Contact your bank immediately if you think you have been scammed and tell the police.

Thousands of work experience placements are set to be provided by the UK’s major retail brands as part of a broader government push to tackle youth unemployment.

Named "Opening Shift", the initiative will connect young universal credit claimants directly with opportunities at businesses including Tesco, John Lewis, Curry’s and Costa Coffee.

Around 40 retailers have signed up so far, pledging more than 11,000 placements that last between two to four weeks.

Participating firms will also offer an interview at the end of the placement, aiming to recruit as many candidates as possible.

The placements will be voluntary, and young people will keep receiving their universal credit where eligible.

Organised by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) and the British Retail Consortium (BRC), the programme forms part of plans to create 100,000 jobs for young people not in education, employment or training – so-called "Neets" – before the next election.

Speaking during a visit to John Lewis in London’s Oxford Street, Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said the scheme would offer young Neets "huge" benefits.

He said: “They are quite often caught in a bind of no experience, no job.

“About 60% of Neets have never had a job and this cuts through that.”

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden (centre) during a visit to John Lewis in London’s Oxford Street ( PA )

He added: “Once they get that (experience), the chances of getting hired in a long-term paid job go up hugely, every senior manager of a business tells you that.”

BRC chief executive Helen Dickinson said: “Retail is coming to the rescue for tens of thousands of young people struggling to take their first step on the career ladder.

“Too many are trapped in a no experience, no job doom loop. High-quality work experience is essential to fix this problem and Opening Shift is a major contribution to delivering it.”

An estimated 981,000 people aged between 16 and 24 were classified as Neet between April and June 2026.

While this was a slight fall from the more than 1 million Neets in the first quarter of the year, the figure remains 30,000 higher than in 2025.

Ministers have commissioned Blair-era cabinet minister Alan Milburn to come up with recommendations for cutting youth unemployment, and recruited former M&S chairman Marc Bolland to work with businesses to get young people into jobs.

Mr Bolland, who played a key role in organising the BRC work experience programme, said the announcement created “thousands more opportunities for young people to build a future in one of Britain’s biggest industries”.

Mr McFadden said he hoped to expand the scheme beyond the retail sector, encouraging other businesses to make similar commitments.

He said: “Together, we can say that this is a cause for the UK, that we are not simply going to sit back and accept the situation where 1 million young people are not engaged in productive economic activity.”

News.title: The Chancellor’s speech, as it happened
News.content:
John Healey failed to rule out tax rises at next month’s Budget in his first major speech as Chancellor.

Mr Healey also sought to blame Liz Truss and her mini-Budget in 2022 for the high borrowing costs being paid by the Treasury.

During a speech in Coventry, the Chancellor said he would be “honest” about the need to control public spending during his time in Number 11.

He was speaking days after the cost of government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007.

It was also overshadowed by Jaguar Land Rover announcing plans to cut 4,000 jobs in the face of “intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty”.

Read our report on the Chancellor’s speech.

News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

News.title: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions
News.content:
This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

News.title: Antonelli walks on water while Hamilton rages from mountaintop
News.content:
The 20-year-old also benefited from a perfectly-timed (from his perspective at least) mid-race virtual safety car when Lance Stroll retired his Aston Martin, which allowed Antonelli a cheap stop to switch to fresh mediums while Russell stayed out on used hards. But at some point you just have to take your hat off to the youngster.

Antonelli was irresistible. He had already surged from 19th on the grid to 12th by the time the red flag came out at the end of lap 2. He was up to sixth a couple of laps after the race resumed. And by lap 18 of a 53-lap race, he had passed Russell for the lead for the first time. That is some going.

Having caught up to Russell, the two Mercedes drivers engaged in an entertaining battle for a few laps, the pair of them yo-yoing in and out of the lead before Russell got past Antonelli on lap 23 and managed to make it stick.

But the key moment of the race came on lap 27 when Stroll stopped at the first chicane and the VSC came out. For Antonelli, the decision to switch to fresh mediums was clear. He was going to struggle to make it to the end of the race. Far better to drop a few positions and fight back on fresh rubber.

For Russell, it was far trickier. He was in the lead of the race. He was on hard tyres which he knew could get to the end of the race. And he also had the problem of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who at the time he was struggling to shake off.

Mercedes chose to keep Russell out there. In hindsight, it may have been the wrong decision. Had he stopped at that point, he would at least have stayed ahead of Antonelli, and on the same tyres. By staying out, he kept the lead but found himself relentlessly hunted down by the Italian.

By lap 49, the Italian had caught up to him. Antonelli botched his first attempt at reclaiming the lead, going wide onto the gravel at the first chicane. But he made no mistake one lap later as Russell was once again left licking his wounds.

News.content:
“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

News.title: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw
News.content:
A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

News.title: Relentless Springboks give All Blacks 15 minutes of hell to lead series
News.content:
There will be no repeat of the All Blacks historic Test series victory in South Africa 30 years ago, after the home side ruthlessly ensured they will lead 2-1 going into the concluding weekend.

And the manner in which the Springboks blew away their fierce rivals in the last 15 minutes made Rassie Eramus’s men overwhelming favourites to finish the job in America next Saturday.

However, there were passages of this brutal battle that suggested that Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry could still produce a finale worthy of the billing if New Zealand can learn the lessons from this brutal encounter at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

There was a late Kiwi try to give the scoreboard a humdinger hue but Erasmus’s side were well deserving of their second victory in as many Saturdays over their fierce rivals, and credit to the South Africa coach for outwitting counterpart Dave Rennie without needing to change his starting XV just before the kick-off, like he did seven days before.

Amazing what one can do with a simple but chilling game plan. The old scoundrel knew that if he slowed it down and let his scrum walk round the All Blacks scrum that his backs would have the precious space.

Yet, however it might feel away from Springbok turf, New Zealand will still fancy their chances of levelling it, especially after matching their opponents’ haul of four tries. Their fly-half, Ruben Love, missed five simple-enough points and until that last quarter it was an even contest. Yet, as it tends to, South Africa’s physical intensity and their almighty scrum eventually prevailed.

News.title: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

Sports.title: Non-league Brit goalie set to become king of Ugandan kingdom after royal selection
Sports.content:
A NON-LEAGUE goalie could be set to be the safe hands of a royal crown — after being chosen as the next king of a Ugandan kingdom.

George Desmond Kamurasi — who plays in the ninth tier of English football — has been selected by a committee to be the ruler of the Tooro people.



It comes after his cousin, King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, 34, died while being treated for cancer.

British national George, 36, known as “Big G”, captains SE Dons in the Southern Counties East League Premier Division.



Video clips show him giving fiery team talks at the club in Bexleyheath, South East London.

But George, who lives with his wife and son, is reported to be reluctant to leave the capital to accept the role.



In Uganda, some are keen on his “no-nonsense” style, while others have questioned how a man brought up in the UK can represent them.

The funeral of King Oyo, who ascended the throne when he was only three in 1995, takes place this weekend.

His royal roots run deep, with his grandfather King George Rukidi III having welcomed the late Queen Elizabeth during her 1954 tour of Uganda.

But there is one final twist, Kamurasi could miss the king’s funeral because it clashes with his football team’s cup fixture.



SE Dons play in the 9th division of the English football pyramid and are based Bexleyheath, southeast London.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland reveals bizarre wood-chopping hobby helps him relax as Man City star admits burnout fears
Sports.content:
ERLING HAALAND is ready to set the Champions League alight again.

But the Manchester City superstar, 26, admits he does worry about burning out after his World Cup heroics.



Haaland enjoyed only a couple of weeks’ downtime after his seven-goal summer.

And the Norwegian revealed even when he’s relaxing he’s red hot – as he loves nothing more than chopping fire wood.



Haaland reckons swinging his axe helps to clear his mind and chill.

On his YouTube channel, Haaland spoke about how he likes to pass his free time in an outbuilding in the grounds of his Cheshire mansion.

He told fans: “This is where the magic happens. This is where I chop the wood and burn it.

“It gives me peace in my mind, that’s what I like about it. Chop wood, burn it and relax, alone.

“It’s really good for me, it clears my mind. So this is what I’m doing when I’m home.

“Looking at fire is pure peace. It’s one of my favourite things to look at. Nature is life.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“People will think I’m joking but this is actually what I’m doing. I’ve been doing it for as long as I can remember.

“We used to do it in my cabin back in Norway. They do it in the mountains there — cozy moments, burn some wood.

“I like to do it outside, inside but I prefer this camping vibe because it’s peaceful and calm. That’s why I love it.”

And he revealed he got into chopping wood thanks to some words of wisdom from his dad, former Leeds and City star Alfie — who, ironically, also played for Nottingham Forest.

Haaland said: “My father taught me this — that firewood makes you hot several times.



“First you need to chop the tree down, which makes you hot.

“Then you need to chop it up, makes you hot. Put them to dry, makes you hot.

“Go and get it and bring it inside, makes you hot. And then you burn it. Six times you’re getting hot, from that one tree.”



Spending time in his cabin is helping Haaland to process a “crazy” summer for him with Norway at the World Cup.

He was one of the stars of the show at his first international tournament and even helped to send Brazil home before his nation bowed out with a 2-1 extra-time defeat by England in the quarter-finals.

Pictures of Haaland and his team-mates doing their Viking ‘rowing’ celebration after victories became enduring images of the tournament.

But the target man admits fearing his feats Stateside could lead to burnout at City.

Haaland was allowed to miss City’s pre-season Far East tour by new boss Enzo Maresca, so only returned to training in the middle of last month.



And although he has already bagged three goals in three games this season to help City to a perfect record so far, he is concerned ahead of what promises to be another gruelling campaign.

Ahead of their Champions League opener in Porto, Haaland said: “Sometimes we need a break as well. I’ve never been in this situation before — I never played a World Cup so I don’t know how it is.

“Doing so well at the World Cup, the row. Just everything, how it worked together, it’s just crazy.



“It feels like we won the World Cup, in some way. The whole world was talking about the row, on holidays. Even now, meeting people in the street.

“When I came back it was like, ‘Wow, it’s good to be home’, but so much had happened and I hadn’t digested it.

“I normally have a bit of pre-season but this time, just nothing.

“The physical side will come but you need to be sharp mentally as well and that’s not easy.

“We need to have that eager feeling to go back but we don’t because there is no time to properly stay away from football because there are so many games.



“I’m not complaining because it’s still a positive thing that you get to play football throughout the whole year and live off it.”

It was seven years ago this month the striker first announced himself on European club football’s biggest stage.

On his Champions League debut, he bagged a first-half hat-trick for RB Salzburg against Genk and has barely stopped since.

He has 57 goals in 58 appearances in the competition and sits joint-ninth with Bayern Munich legend Thomas Muller in the all-time top-scorers list.

Haaland is just two behind Andriy Shevchenko, with Ruud van Nistelrooy a further goal ahead.



Lionel Messi is the fastest player to reach 60 Champions League goals.

But he needed 80 matches to reach that tally — meaning the Etihad idol has 21 games to find just three more goals.

But Maresca plans to keep a close eye on Haaland, and the rest of City’s World Cup stars.



He said: “It’s not easy for Erling or most of the players that play for club and the international team.

“The risk is there can be an injury and we need players 100 per cent.”

Sports.title: Chelsea ‘nearly signed former Premier League flop, 29, to replace Enzo Fernandez’ days after he had contract ripped up
Sports.content:
CHELSEA considered Swansea flop Renato Sanches as a potential replacement for Enzo Fernandez, reports suggest.

Sanches, 29, became a free agent after Paris Saint-Germain terminated his contract following four ill-fated years that included three hapless loan stints at Roma, Benfica and Panathinaikos.



According to Foot Mercato, however, the Blues were, “for a time”, interested in the midfielder.

The same source claims the ex-Portugal international ticked “many boxes” in the eyes of the West Londoners’ decision makers.



Chelsea listed Sanches among their transfer targets notably due to his top-flight experience and immediate availability in the closing stages of a tumultuous summer transfer window.

Xabi Alonso saw star midfielder Fernandez, 25, move to Manchester City on deadline day in a joint-Premier League record £125million deal.

Chelsea thought they had Monaco star Lamine Camara sealed as the Argentina international’s replacement but his club sensationally pulled the plug AFTER the window had closed.

The French giants thought star striker Folarin Balogun would move to Everton and didn’t want to part with yet another key player after Maghnes Akliouche went to PSG.

However, Monaco were left with egg on their face as Balogun opted against joining the Toffees and missed out on some much-needed profit as Camara also stayed, much to the anger of Chelsea.

The Premier League giants moved quickly for a potential last-minute alternative to fill in for Fernandez.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Reports suggested ex-Liverpool and Newcastle star Georginio Wijnaldum was mooted after his departure from Al-Ettifaq but nothing came of it and he went to Al-Ittihad.

And thus, Chelsea almost decided to bring in Sanches despite his dramatic fall from grace, which was littered with injury.

The central midfielder burst onto the scene in 2015 at the age of 18 after rising through Benfica’s ranks and was quickly dubbed football’s next big thing.

That led to a blockbuster move to Bayern Munich a year later but he couldn’t live up to expectations.

That led to a surprise loan stint at Swansea in 2017 that proved to be disastrous as he only managed a mere total of 15 appearances.



One of which saw him committing an unforgettable gaffe as he randomly passed the ball to an advertising board in a match that was funnily enough against Chelsea.

Sanches looked to have regained his old self upon moving to Lille in 2019 as he registered 91 appearances across an impressive three-year stint.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho can seal Champions League history with Real Madrid but must answer burning question
Sports.content:
THERE are managers who crave recognition, attention, the spotlight.

And then there is Jose Mourinho.

A man who believes the football world — maybe even the whole globe — revolves around him.



But if the Portuguese is going to become the first boss to lift the Champions League with three different clubs, it is surely now.

Or, perhaps, continue the journey towards the obscurity which would leave even Mourinho, for all his ego, destitute.



His return to Real Madrid seems to have been scripted as the ultimate redemption story.

The self-styled Special One was hounded out of the Bernabeu 13 years ago, jettisoned as the victim of player power from a dressing room that refused to be told what to do.

Then this summer, recruited once more by Florentino Perez and hailed as the antidote to fix a different Madrid squad that spent last term bickering with the coaching staff and physically taking actual lumps out of each other on the training ground.

We all know the Mourinho story. A force of nature at Porto, Chelsea and Inter Milan — winning the Champions League with the Portuguese and Italian clubs — conquering unlikely peaks while fighting with every fibre of his body.

Yet equally, the fall-out at Madrid, the return to Chelsea that brought a third Premier League crown but internal war, including a fatal public spat with the team doctor and an ignominious exit.

And the short-lived spells at Manchester United, Tottenham, Roma, Fenerbahce and Benfica, a gradual fading of the light that once burned so bright.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

It means this second Madrid incarnation is make or break. While regaining LaLiga supremacy is important to the club, triumphing in Europe is Mourinho’s driving ambition.

The recent three-part Netflix documentary gives an insight into his soul.

Long-held suspicions that he considers himself the inheritor of the navigators, who discovered uncharted lands for colonisation, were confirmed.

But unlike Christopher Columbus, Vasco da Gama and Ferdinand Magellan, Mourinho wanted to dominate old worlds, not conquer new ones. As he admitted: “I wanted to make history — and nothing was going to stop me.”

That has not changed. But neither has time stood still.

Mourinho, 63, is more than two decades older than he was when he ran down the touchline as Porto boss at Old Trafford in 2004, his grey coat flapping.

The chiselled features are no longer quite so sharp, even if the acid tongue remains. But going one beyond the two-club European title feats of old foes Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti, as well as reigning champion Luis Enrique, would cement Mourinho’s status.



In his own words: “Greatness is to be in history.”

Kicking off against former club Inter, in a match which could feature five English players, Mourinho knows all too well the expectations . . . and the opportunity.

While Arsenal have laid down their domestic marker already, the other four Prem clubs are all under new management, while Paris Saint-Germain have two last-gasp draws and a defeat from their opening three Ligue 1 games.

The big question, as ever with Jose, is how he copes when things do not go right.

Mourinh) joined Madrid first time round believing every player was a potential ally but left convinced each of them was the enemy.



Burning question

The tall poppy theory became a self-fulfilling and damaging prophecy. So far, he has been on his best behaviour.

After the surprise 1-0 defeat at Real Betis on Friday, when a dreadful VAR call meant Kylian Mbappe was denied the chance to rectify his spot-kick miss, Mourinho avoided the blame game.

Yet the suspicion is that, if things go wrong, he will target one of his stars, Mbappe, Vinicius Jr — who will harbour doubts after Mourinho’s defence of Benfica winger Gianluca Prestianni’s abusive comments last term — or Jude Bellingham.

In the documentary, Mourinho insists: “I wanted to be loved.”



He does. But he also loves to be hated. The danger is that he finds it increasingly easier to attract the latter than the former. This feels like the final chapter.

No time to hand in chips

JUST three weekends in and the folly of Premier League chiefs refusing to use the World Cup-style connected ball has been exposed.

Spain’s LaLiga, which also uses a Puma ball, has introduced the chip technology this season but bosses decided it was not necessary here. Cue the furore over Neco Williams’ “handball goal” against Tottenham.

The chip would have helped detect any contact with a “non-goalscoring” part of Williams’ body — his arm — allowing VAR Peter Bankes to make an informed decision, rather than taking a punt.

Bankes probably made the right call to disallow the goal — photo stills seem to show Forest’s Williams accidentally handled.



But under the protocols, it’s hard to figure out how he could see it sufficiently to overturn the on-field decision from the camera angles at his disposal.

Using the latest modern technology — good enough for the second-best domestic league in the world — would have shut down the controversy.

Purrfect for Mikel

MIKEL ARTETA was the cat that got the cream on Sunday night. You couldn’t blame him, either, for his purrs of contentment.

The Basque tactician deployed his lexicon of positive adjectives at his team’s outstanding performance.

Arsenal were “exceptional”, “spectacular” and “beautiful”, Ezri Konsa “phenomenal”, Kai Havertz “amazing”, Martin Odegaard “perfect”.



Arteta had two audiences. The one in the Emirates press conference room was secondary.

After Chelsea’s pretensions were put into context, he wanted his words to reverberate around the Etihad — to get Enzo Maresca and his Manchester City team talking.

What a Fox up

A DECADE ago, Leicester were preparing for their first Champions League campaign as Premier League winners.

And five years later, it was Napoli in the Europa League as FA Cup holders. Today, Foxes fans are licking their wounds following the humiliating 4-0 League One home drubbing by Oxford.

Boss Russell Martin looks like a one-trick pony that hasn’t actually got a trick, with the club’s very future unclear and League Two football next term more than possible. Never forget, nothing in football is permanent.



Hands on

UEFA referees’ boss Roberto Rosetti accepts there have been far too many handball penalties awarded in recent seasons.

The talk is of alignment across Europe and “clear evidence for interventions, not marginal and microscopic reviews”.

See how long that lasts!

Sports.title: New footage emerges of Nottingham Forest’s controversial disallowed goal vs Spurs – but it wasn’t available to VAR
Sports.content:
A NEW camera angle has surfaced of Nottingham Forest’s controversially disallowed goal against Tottenham — but it is still unlikely to end the VAR row.

Forest and Spurs played out a dramatic goalless draw at the City Ground on Saturday, which saw Roberto De Zerbi’s side pick up their first Premier League point of the season after losing their opening two matches.



However, Nottingham thought they scored the winner on 67 minutes when Neco Williams bravely lunged to the ball head first to meet captain Morgan Gibbs-White‘s lob.

Williams, 25, tried to protect his physical wellbeing by placing his arms on his face to protect himself from Tottenham star Sandro Tonali’s flying boot.



Referee Craig Pawson awarded the goal but VAR Peter Bankes stepped in to give a handball – leaving Forest and fans across the country incredulous.

Now, fresh footage appears to show the ball DID his Williams’ arm on its way into the back of the net.



But it is still not totally conclusive.

Incredibly, this angle wasn’t even shown to the VAR during the game.

The incident has been replayed over and over this weekend as fans search for conclusive proof of what happened.

Some have even claimed that even if the goal was ruled out, Forest should have been awarded a penalty for Tonali‘s kick at Williams’ head.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

PGMOL chief refereeing officer Howard Webb backed Bankes but plans to lobby for the law to be changed regarding accidental handballs.

The rule states that a goal must be axed if the ball goes into the net off a player’s hand or arm – even if completely accidental.

Webb said: “It is a law I would definitely look to change. So Pro Ref and the Premier League are going to try and lobby for that to be changed.

“At the moment, if the ball goes into the goal off your hand, accidentally or otherwise, you have to disallow that.

“And if it touches your hand accidentally or ­otherwise and then [you] score with your foot, you have to disallow the goal.



“The problem is that forces VARs on every goal to look at what body part the ball went in off.

“Most times it’s dead obvious it has come off the head or the foot. But there’s a fair number of situations where it is close to hitting the arm. The VAR has to look at it from different angles.

“There might be six angles focusing in on the player and the first three might not be conclusive.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“If you were only to penalise when the attacker deliberately handles the ball or makes himself unjustifiably big — and not have that forensic examination which p***** people off — you could ‘check complete’ it more quickly.”



Forest are currently without a win in the Premier League this season having amassed a total of two points from their first three matches.

Sports.title: Declan Rice called out for 'cheating' as Graeme Souness launches new attack on Arsenal star
Sports.content:
Declan Rice called out for 'cheating' as Graeme Souness launches new attack on Arsenal star

Declan Rice has earned huge plaudits across the course of his career but Graeme Souness continues to highlight the limitations in the Arsenal and England midfielder's game

View 2 Images Declan Rice has been told he "isn't the complete midfielder"

Graeme Souness has again taken aim at Declan Rice - accusing the Arsenal midfielder of playing "old man's football".

‌



The England star remains the most expensive player in the Gunners' history and has been crucial in them morphing into one of Europe's elite forces. Rice has proved a dominant force for club and country, helping Arsenal win the Premier League last season, but Souness is still not convinced by his quality and doesn't have him in the top bracket of midfielders.

‌



He has taken issue with the position the 27-year-old adopts during games. Souness cited how Rice can often be seen as one of the deepest Arsenal players on the pitch, giving him more time as he plays almost as a central defender, with the ex-Sky Sports pundit suggesting he's "cheating" with his positioning as he continued his brutal assessment.

‌



He said on Piers Morgan's new Football Uncensored show: "How many times do you see him as the last man with the ball. In the build-up, he's last man. He's sitting between two centre-halves or between the centre-half and the full-back. He's last man. A lot of the time, he doesn't play in midfield.

"In my second or third home game (of my career), I went into the back four like all midfield players do today. It's old man's football. It's cheating. An old man's way of playing midfield. You get the ball under no pressure and you play it out to the full-back."

‌



Souness has previously claimed that Rice's game is limited, despite the clear influence he's had on Arsenal and England over the years. The Liverpool great suggests that, for a midfielder, he's playing too far back to truly have an impact on the outcome.

"He (Rice) plays too deep to affect the game," he continued. "I don't think he's got enough football. Let me tell you what he can do. He's the best defensive midfielder in the country right now, he smells danger. But then again, he's back there all the time.

"He's not a midfield player then is he? I think he may be a centre-half. The ball travels faster than you do. I see him run with the ball 30 yards and pass it square. He's a lovely kicker of the ball and opens his body up well, there's nothing to dislike about him. But modern players are a bit precious. Criticism doesn't fall easily on these (players') shoulders. He isn't the complete midfield player."

Sports.title: VAR row takes fresh twist as new image of Nottingham Forest disallowed goal released
Sports.content:
VAR row takes fresh twist as new image of Nottingham Forest disallowed goal released

Nottingham Forest's disallowed goal on Saturday has caused plenty of debate after Neco Williams was pinned for handball - but a new image has shed light on the saga

View 2 Images Nottingham Forest were left fuming after VAR ruled out their goal against Tottenham

A new picture shows the ball DID hit Neco Williams’ arm - but might not end the VAR row over Nottingham Forest ’s disallowed goal.

‌



Williams bundled the ball over the line but video assistant referee Peter Bankes disallowed the goal even though Forest boss Oliver Glasner insisted there was no proof.

‌



But a still picture does show the ball hitting Forest defender Williams’ arm which is why it was disallowed in Saturday’s goalless draw with Tottenham, denying the home side a precious win.

‌



However, the picture was not available to Bankes when he made his decision to intervene which then saw referee Craig Pawson disallow the goal.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Referees' body, Pro Ref, are comfortable that the correct decision was made and that Bankes is an experienced VAR who also knows tell-tale signs like a ripple of the shirt.

‌



Refs boss Howard Webb has overseen a “lighter touch” this season from VAR which should result in less interventions with the strict instructions that officials should not get involved unless they are sure. Pro Ref are backing the officials over this decision which has caused a backlash from Forest who have history on ref rows.

This time, Glasner said: “I think the VAR can't intervene when he is guessing. It was not clear and obvious. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high, which is why this is a wrong intervention.”

View 2 Images A new angle has shown that the ball did strike Neco Williams' arm

‌



The Forest boss also claimed: "I think it was a clear penalty when Neco Williams was fouled by Mo Kudus. We didn't feel that some decisions were in our favor today. If it's not 100% clear, stick to the on-field decisions. This is the inconsistency today. I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood."

The stats show that there have been just two subjective interventions this season which is a ratio of 0.06 after 30 games compared to 0.15 last season.

Arsenal had a goal ruled out by VAR in their win over Chelsea on Sunday. It came when they were trailing 1-0 but replays showed the officials were again right to step in.

Sports.title: Ederson gives fresh take on Man Utd medical after £35m transfer fell through
Sports.content:
Ederson gives fresh take on Man Utd medical after £35m transfer fell through

Manchester United had agreed a deal to sign Atalanta midfielder Ederson before changing their mind and pursuing other targets

View 2 Images Manchester United's summer transfer swoop for Ederson fell through after the player undertook a medical. (Image: (Photo by Danilo Di Giovanni/Getty Images))

Manchester United's summer transfer target Ederson has insisted that the injuries which cost him his place in the Brazilian national team squad this summer were nothing serious, with the Reds also walking away from a deal to bring the Atalanta midfielder to Old Trafford.

‌



United had struck an agreement worth £35m plus a further £4m in add-ons, to secure the services of the 27-year-old as a replacement for departing midfielder Casemiro, who left the club when his contract expired.

‌



However, medical examinations revealed a 'significant' knee problem, which proved sufficient for the Reds to pull the plug on the transfer. Michael Carrick's side subsequently moved to bring in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba, while Ederson penned a fresh Atalanta deal.

‌



The midfielder has committed his future to the Serie A outfit until the summer of 2031 and has spoken candidly about the fitness issues that disrupted his summer.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"I'm very well, as I've always been, actually. Physically, I can't complain. I've always been very blessed in that regard, I've always been well," he told Trivela.

‌



"The injuries that affected my call-ups were minor. They kept me out for a few days, and I was just unlucky that they happened very close to the call-ups.

"That's why I always came back very quickly. I've never had any kind of injury that kept me out for a long time."

View 2 Images Ederson's move to Manchester United fell through. (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Ederson has emphasised that he returned to the Italian club ahead of schedule in a bid to rebuild his fitness following the tournament, stating the process went without a hitch.

He added: "I did the whole preparation without any problems, all the tests, and started the season as always. I'm very well to continue the season. And Atalanta know me very well."

‌



Ederson has taken on the Atalanta captaincy and featured in all four of their fixtures this season so far, emphasising his strong bond with the club.

The midfielder said: "I always spoke a lot with the club, I have an excellent relationship here. Whenever this happened, with enquiries and offers, I asked what Atalanta's intention was, what the project was, whether they were thinking of selling me, and they never thought about selling me."

This marks the second occasion this summer that Ederson has discussed his collapsed transfer to United. Speaking last month prior to Atalanta's Europa Conference League play-off tie with Hapoel Tel Aviv regarding the unsuccessful move to United, he said: "I honestly don't know what happened.

"I always had interest from other clubs, and I could've gone to another English side. The tests went well, I don't know what changed.

"I've been with Atalanta for four years and always played. I could've just waited to see what happened, but the great rapport with the club convinced me to stay and sign a new contract."

Sports.title: Harry Kane tipped to join 'exclusive little club' and end 25-year wait with Ballon d'Or win
Sports.content:
Harry Kane tipped to join 'exclusive little club' and end 25-year wait with Ballon d'Or win

Harry Kane is set to be bang in contention for the Ballon d'Or, with Michael Owen already tipping him to win the award ahead of the likes of Kylian Mbappe

View 2 Images Harry Kane smiles as he warms up ahead of the 2026 World Cup football tournament third-place match between France and England at the Miami Stadium in Miami on July 18, 2026. (Photo by ROBERTO SCHMIDT / AFP via Getty Images) (Image: Getty)

Harry Kane has been told he deserves to join an “exclusive little club” - and be crowned winner of the Ballon D’Or.

‌



England captain Kane, 33, will discover his rivals for the prestigious crown on Tuesday when the 30 name shortlist is unveiled for one of the biggest honours in football.

‌



Kane is the red-hot bookies’ favourite after his record-breaking season when he scored 73 goals for club and would be England’s first winner in a quarter of a century.

‌



Michael Owen was the last winner in 2001 and believes Kane - who will be up against the likes of Rodri, Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi - deserves to win the award which will be handed out in London on October 26.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The Former Liverpool striker insists that Kane has had a “phenomenal season” and is the “best finisher on the planet. Owen said: “Let's hope that all that means that you're going to get a huge shout of winning the Ballon D’Or. I would welcome you with open arms to join our exclusive little club.”

‌



The Ballon D’Or often goes to a player from the winning nation in World Cup year but there is not an outstanding candidate and there is a strong feeling it could - and should - be Kane’s year, especially after a hugely successful season with Bayern Munich.

Kane, in an interview with TNT Sports, said: “I'm here now, and I'm winning awards like the Golden Shoe. And the Ballon d’Or is the same. Of course, now it's out of my hands in terms of it's down to the voters and the people who decide it.

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe also has his sights set on the prestigious award (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



“The season I had was my best season by far, and we have to wait and see this. It's a weird one because I'm already focussed on this season now and the next season and thinking how can I be better, how can I improve. But also I want to appreciate what I did. Time will tell.”

Real Madrid star Mbappe is also banging the drum for his own cause as he is dreaming of winning it for the first time even though he did not win any trophies.

Mbappe said: “I think when you play for Real Madrid, the best club in the world, people associate you with this award. There are many people that speak about me and the Ballon d'Or. Of course I've made history in the most important competition. Maybe it's a good year for this but people can vote according to what they think.”

Sports.title: Edu's venture after Arsenal exit 'not what he envisaged' as Nottingham Forest errors prove costly
Sports.content:
Edu's time at Nottingham Forest is officially over, with the Brazilian leaving his role as Global Head of Football.

Almost two years on from leaving his role at Arsenal with his stock at an all-time high, Edu's gamble to move elsewhere for a broader remit has not quite paid off. The former Gunner had worked impressively in tandem with Mikel Arteta as the duo combined to make the north Londoners a force in the Premier League once more. But, shortly after a second successive season where Arsenal finished as runners-up to Manchester City, Edu left the Emirates.

He headed to the City Ground to work under Evangelos Marinakis, with a desire to work in a multi-club model seen as a huge pull, with Edu also overseeing Olympiacos and Rio Ave.

However his work in Nottingham failed to produce the necessary results and he's been removed from his role. The news has been a long time coming - The 48-year-old had been sidelined for months and hasn't attended a match since February or set foot in the City Ground or training facility since early March.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The Telegraph reports that the work assigned to Edu was not what he envisaged when he took on the job. Edu himself accepts that he struggled to foster relationships with key members of Marinakis' staff, which ultimately made his job more challenging.

The decline in his relationship with Nuno Espirito Santo was also well documented, leading to the Portuguese leaving the City Ground. Last year's disaster campaign saw Forest go through four managers - Nuno, Ange Postecoglou, Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira as the club narrowly avoided the drop. Oliver Glasner is now at the helm.

The transfer decisions taken by Edu failed to push the club on, after they had finished seventh and qualified for Europe in 2025. The former Arsenal chief was responsible for several transfer calls that failed to pay dividends - he led the pursuit of Igor Jesus from Brazilian club Botafogo.

‌



View 3 Images Edu's difficult relationship with Nuno Espirito Santo was well documented (Image: Visionhaus, Visionhaus/Getty Images)

The £37.5million signing of Omari Hutchinson, plus loan deals for Douglas Luiz and Oleksandr Zinchenko, were all influenced by Edu, but only three of those four players remain at the club.

Adding James McAtee from Manchester City was seen as a real coup, but the young midfielder has struggled to push on, in part owing to the constant managerial upheaval that has impacted on a host of players. Being on the outer meant that the club's summer transfer business was conducted with other key figures.

When Edu quit Arsenal he claimed: "This was an incredibly hard decision to make. Now it is time to pursue a different challenge."

‌



View 3 Images Omari Hutchinson was one of several Nottingham Forest signings who have not delivered (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Whilst at the Emirates Edu, who was part of the Invincibles that won the title in 2004, helped assemble a huge bulk of the team that would go on to win the Premier League last season. He was responsible for signing Martin Odegaard, Ben White, Gabriel and the club-record capture Declan Rice.

But since leaving the Arsenal wheel has continued to turn and they've been able to add more star quality, which now leaves them with the best squad in the league by some distance. Andrea Berta, effectively Edu's replacement, has continued to conduct the club's business.

Edu's stint at the City Ground will leave him scarred and his upwardly mobile status was always going to be assessed after joining Forest, which in itself was by no means a step forward, if anything its set him back.

‌

Sports.title: Michael Carrick should not be 'disappointed' with Man Utd setback - he should be angry
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick should not be 'disappointed' with Man Utd setback - he should be angry

The Man Utd boss has come under fire for saying his team's start to the season has 'not been that bad' and needs to get on the front foot in the Champions League and Manchester derby

View 3 Images Michael Carrick saw victory snatched away at Everton

It was once accepted wisdom that if, as an elite football manager, you do not get too euphoric when things are going well or too despondent when things are going slightly awry, then it is a good trait to have. Not any more.

‌



That is why Michael Carrick was probably ill-advised to say Manchester United’s start to the Premier League season has ‘not been that bad.’ Even though it has, er, not been that bad.

‌



Carrick’s character is not going to change but, like it or not, perception is important in the modern managerial game. Supporters do not like a shrug of the shoulders.

‌



Carrick said he was ‘disappointed’ with the way the game ended at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday. That does not cut it these days.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Arne Slot found that out last season. One of the Dutchman’s issues was that he became eminently reasonable in his dissection of unfavourable results.

‌



More often than not, Carrick quite reasonably said, Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ strike does not go in. In fact, that is a totally reasonable thing to say.

In 334 appearances in professional football, Maitland-Niles has now scored 12 goals. He has never scored a goal like that in his professional life - and will never score one like it again.

View 3 Images Benjamin Sesko thought he was the matchwinner at Hill Dickinson Stadium (Image: Getty Images)

‌



But what Carrick should have been saying is that he was angry United did not go for Everton’s jugular after Bryan Mbeumo’s goal early in the second half. He should have been saying that he was angry United did not create a chance in the 40 minutes that followed Mbeumo’s goal.

And you can bet he was angry. Yes, United were denied a win by two freakishly good hits, but they were also complacent. And while they might have finished a decent third in the Premier League last season, they have nothing to be complacent about.

Of course, it is way too early to read too much into the start of a season. Liverpool were the only team to record three wins from their opening three matches last season.

‌



In fact, Slot’s team won five out five to kick off their defence. We all know what happened after that. When he looks ahead to Thursday’s Champions League game against Sabah, Carrick should get on the front foot.

View 3 Images Matheus Cunha does not look like a natural number nine (Image: Getty Images)

No, he cannot change his character but he can be a bit more expressive. When he has watched the Everton game back, he will know it was a badly missed opportunity, regardless of the fact that only an unusually brilliant goal denied them all three points.

‌



And he will say that. He will demand a response in the Champions League and then against Manchester City at Old Trafford next Sunday.

The game against Sabah is a good opportunity for Carrick. The feeling from the Everton match and the statistics suggest that Benjamin Sesko should be given a starting chance as the central striker.

Matheus Cunha is, quite clearly, not a natural number nine. Sesko, quite clearly, is a natural number nine. He certainly brings an extra dimension when it comes to aggression. And that is what this United team needs. More aggression … from the top down.

Sports.title: Joey Barton to spend Christmas in prison after trial adjourned until next year
Sports.content:
Joey Barton to spend Christmas in prison after trial adjourned until next year

Joey Barton was charged with causing grievous bodily harm with intent, to which he pleaded not guilty, after an alleged serious assault near a golf club in March

View 4 Images Joey Barton (Image: PA)

Joey Barton is due to spend Christmas in prison at HMP Liverpool after a bail application on his behalf was refused. The former Premier League footballer was due to face trial at Liverpool Crown Court last week, but the case was adjourned until March 8 next year.

‌



Barton, 44, was charged with causing grievous bodily harm with intent in connection with an alleged serious assault in March. The alleged victim, Kevin Lynch, was taken to hospital in a serious but stable condition.

‌



He was said to have sustained injuries to his face and ribs. Barton has been refused bail since his arrest.

‌



View 4 Images Joey Barton was initially denied bail in March (Image: PA)

Defence counsel Tim Forte KC applied for bail on his behalf during an hour-long hearing this afternoon (Monday 7 October), but the bid was refused. Barton appeared via video link to HMP Liverpool, wearing a grey Columbia fleece and glasses.

He appeared in the dock of courtroom 42 on Wednesday (2 September), which was his 44th birthday, when the case was adjourned. That is when Judge David Potter further remanded him into custody while proceedings continue.

‌



Judge Potter said: "Mr Barton, your case will next be mentioned on December the 11th. In the meantime, you are remanded in custody through to the next date."

View 4 Images Police at Huyton and Prescot Golf Club following the alleged assault (Image: Liverpool Echo)

That date in December is when the pre-trial review is scheduled. The expectation is that Barton's trial will last for up to a fortnight.

‌



He therefore faces a year in custody after already spending six months inside, with another six-month wait following the case's adjournment to March 8. Barton was wearing glasses, a navy blue suit and tie with a blue shirt and sporting short, greying hair.

Judge Potter told him in the dock: "Mr Barton, I have now fixed your trial to take place on Monday, the 8th of March. In the meantime, you are remanded in custody."

View 4 Images Mr Lynch is the headteacher of an independent school set up for students with additional educational needs

Article continues below

The court previously heard Lynch, 51, had been socialising with Barton at Huyton and Prescot Golf Club on March 8 before the alleged assault. Lynch is a former non-league football manager and was said to have been found covered in blood on Fairway, close to the club's entrance.

He managed City of Liverpool, Marine and Prescot Cables, and, away from football, founded NexGen Academy in Dovecot. He is the headteacher of the school for children with additional needs.

Barton is from Huyton but is now of Fox Bank Close in Widnes. He most recently hosted a podcast.

Sports.title: Rybakina too strong for Osaka as Zheng stuns Swiatek at US Open
Sports.content:
Elena Rybakina cruised into the US Open quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Naomi Osaka to keep her push for the world No 1 ranking on track.

Rybakina will reclaim the top spot if she reaches the semi-finals, and after dismantling two-time champion Osaka on Louis Armstrong, she has every reason to believe she can go all the way and lift the US Open trophy.

It took the second seed just over 20 minutes to wrap up the first set 6-1 before securing a decisive break midway through the second to quell a resurgent Osaka and seal an emphatic 6-1 6-4 victory.

"I played really well today. I was feeling the ball was really good from my side," the former Wimbledon champion said. "I was a bit lucky in some moments, found some lines, but super happy with the performance.

"Naomi is a tough opponent. I knew no matter the score I needed to focus on each ball as everything can change quickly. She is also a great player. I am glad how I played today.

"I want to be world No 1. I don't know anyone who wouldn't wish for that. It is one of my goals.

"I don't know what will happen in my next match but if I serve well, as I did today, I think I have all the chances. Hopefully it goes my way."

Rybakina's level is 'ridiculous'

Sky Sports Tennis' Laura Robson:

"Rybakina's level is just ridiculous.

"The crowd were keen to keep the match going but she silences them. She had the answer to every question Osaka asked of her.

"From the first ball, Rybakina led that. Cross-court rallies, Rybakina led that, too. There was just no area where Osaka could find breathing room."

Zheng stages epic comeback as Swiatek implodes

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Iga Swiatek's match against Qinwen Zheng at the US Open

Rybakina will face Qinwen Zheng in the last eight after the Chinese star produced a second epic comeback in as many days at the US Open, stunning former champion Iga Swiatek to reach the quarter-finals for the third time.

Two days after saving match point while trailing 5-0 in the third set against Madison Keys, Zheng mounted another remarkable fightback on Arthur Ashe.

Swiatek won the first five games, but Zheng simply refused to roll over, winning the next seven to clinch the opening set before overpowering her shellshocked opponent to complete an astonishing 7-5 6-3 victory.

A stunned Swiatek never recovered, with the 2022 champion leaving the court in tears as her campaign unravelled in unthinkable fashion.

The former world No 4, who came through qualifying after being sidelined by a long-term elbow injury, became the first qualifier to reach the quarter-finals since Emma Raducanu won the tournament in 2021.

Image: Qinwen Zheng has matched her best ever performance at the US Open by reaching the quarter-finals

Zheng relishes return to the big stage

"I started the match not so well but I found my rhythm," Zheng said.

"It has been a long, long time since I played on a centre court and I really appreciate being here on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

"I took it point by point and little by little I started to play better and find my game.

"I even forgot the score at 4-5 in the first set, which showed I was focused. To come back from 0-5 is not lucky, that's all I can say."

Image: Qinwen Zheng is the reigning Olympic champion and former world No 4 (Associated Press)

'One of the great comebacks'

Sky Sports Tennis' Jonathan Overend:

"It's a straight-set win but it's one of the great comebacks. Go figure. How's that possible? Zheng made it happen.

"Two games in a row, 5-0 down in sets. She got the win against Madison Keys to get the first set today [Monday], before completing victory against Swiatek for only the second time in her career."

"The Chinese dream lives on as the qualifier makes it into the final eight."

Potapova in tears after late injury in Andreeva defeat

Anastasia Potapova was in floods of tears as her stay in New York came to an end.

The 25-year-old Austrian won the first set against fifth seed Mirra Andreeva, but, at 5-3 down in the third she badly twisted her knee chasing a forehand down.

Potapova had the knee heavily strapped up and bravely finished the match, but did not win another point as French Open champion Andreeva triumphed 5-7 6-4 6-3.

"Anastasia is a good friend, and seeing what a battle we have and then seeing her fall is not easy," said Russian teenager Andreeva.

"It's not the way you want to finish the match. I just told her she is playing amazing and I'm sure she'll come back even stronger, she's a warrior."

Sports.title: Usyk's camp dismiss Fury's offer to be 'backup plan' for Joshua fight
Sports.content:
Oleksandr Usyk's manager has dismissed Tyson Fury's call for a third fight with the Ukrainian amid continued doubt over an all-British heavyweight showdown with Anthony Joshua.

With protracted negotiations over a long-awaited Fury-Joshua bout being held up by a dispute over where the fight would take place, Fury took to social media on Monday to say he was looking for a new opponent.

Fury said he wants a third fight with Usyk, who became undisputed heavyweight champion as he beat Fury twice on points in 2024.

Responding to Fury's comments in a statement given to Sky Sports News on Monday evening, Usyk's manager Sergey Lapin said: "Usyk is not Tyson's backup plan.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Boxing commentator Adam Smith is confident the British mega-fight between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury can still be agreed in time to take place this year

"If Fury needs an opponent, he should visit the Ready to Fight platform. They can help him find a worthy opponent there.

"Oleksandr is always open to big challenges. But serious intentions are backed by a concrete offer, not statements in the press."

Usyk announced in June that he was vacating the three heavyweight belts he still held at the time, but the 39-year-old said he was not yet retiring, and has recently been linked with a fight against Deontay Wilder.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mayor of London Sadiq Khan has called for Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury to fight in London

Usyk, who holds a perfect 25-0 professional record, claimed successive wins over Joshua in 2021 and 2022, but has become part of the Brit's training team over the last year.

Both Joshua and Fury have signed individual contracts for what was slated to be a November contest, but have yet to agree on where the fight will take place, with speculation suggesting it could be held in New York City.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn says he and his fighter want the contest to take place in London, while Fury says his rival is trying to avoid a bout that has been more than a decade in the making.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eddie Hearn claimed that Anthony Joshua feels a responsibility to UK fight fans that AJ vs Fury should happen in the UK

"This will only lead me to a fight with Oleksandr Usyk," Fury said in a video posted on Instagram.

"Oleksandr you're his [Joshua's] trainer and his sensei and you know he is weak minded... and that he would never fight the Gypsy King which you have had the guts to do twice.

"You got the decisions last time, fair play to you. Good luck to you, let's do it again. Let's run it back in November. The ball is now in your court... do you want to fight me this year, 2026, or are you calling it quits?

"Let me know because I am now looking for a new opponent."

Sports.title: Red Bull's Hadjar to miss Spanish GP as injury absence continue
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar will miss this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid as he continues to recover from a fractured wrist.

Liam Lawson will replace Hadjar for a third successive race as Max Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull, while Yuki Tsunoda continues at Racing Bulls.

Hadjar suffered a hairline fracture in a bone in his wrist during the summer break in a routine workout that involved boxing which forced him to miss the Dutch, Italian and now Spanish Grands Prix.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Isack Hadjar was reinstated to the Monaco podium last week after a Red Bull appeal.

A Red Bull statement said: "After racing for the team in Zandvoort and Monza, Liam will continue to drive alongside Max at this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid.

"The decision has been taken as Isack's recovery continues to progress positively. While he is not yet ready to return to the cockpit, he will be in Madrid supporting the team.

"Everyone at Red Bull Racing looks forward to welcoming Isack back behind the wheel very soon."

Lawson impressively qualified only one tenth behind Verstappen at Zandvoort and finished the Dutch Grand Prix in seventh - a complete contrast to his two Red Bull outings at the start of 2025 before he was dropped.

But, he went out in Q2 at Monza, partly due to being impeded by Oscar Piastri on his best lap. In the race, he started from the pit lane due to engine penalties but made contact with Audi's Nico Hulkenberg at an early standing start restart, so had to change his front wing and recovered to 14th, while Verstappen was on the podium.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liam Lawson sits down with Sky Sports F1's Crofty to reveal his the tracks he'd take with him to a desert island

Tsunoda has produced two solid weekends at Racing Bulls, finishing a place ahead of team-ate Arvid Lindblad in the Dutch Grand Prix, before scoring a point by taking 10th at Monza.

The Monza result looks set to be appealed by rivals Audi over an incident at the standing restart, which saw Tsunoda pull into the wrong grid slot, triggering an extra formation lap.

The 26-year-old, who was dropped by Red Bull last season, expressed hope ahead of the Italian Grand Prix that he could convince someone to give him a seat on the grid in 2027.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Audi have lodged an 'intention to appeal' after Yuki Tsunoda escaped a penalty for this incident at the Italian Grand Prix restart

"I'm free! Would love to hear those calls, but not yet," he said. "It's good that things are going positive, at least.

"Obviously, my primary target is to be in Formula 1. Let's see. In this world anything can happen. At the same time, it's also knowing that it's not easy to have a seat."

Sports.title: Pakistan investigating 'discipline and conduct' in latest twist on crisis tour
Sports.content:
The Pakistan Cricket Board has launched an investigation into "media reports concerning discipline and conduct" amid the team's crisis tour of England.

Pakistan last week took the unprecedented step of sending seven players home and calling up seven after losing heavily at Headingley and Lord's to fall 2-0 down in the three-match series.

Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul have also been replaced, with Mike Hesson, in charge of Pakistan's white-ball sides, and former Australia seamer Ashley Noffke overseeing the third Test at Edgbaston, which begins on Wednesday.

A statement read: "The Pakistan Cricket Board has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the best of day four at Lord's as England thumped Pakistan by 194 runs to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match Test series

"The PCB handles such matters in accordance with its standard procedures. The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration.

"At this stage, any speculative reports or unverified claims circulating on certain platforms, particularly those originating from hostile external sources, should not be regarded as credible."

The banished senior players included Salman Ali Agha - who captained Pakistan in the first Test before being dropped for the second - wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq, who did not bat in either innings after suffering a low-grade calf strain in the field.

Former captain Shahid Afridi described the PCB's decision to make sweeping alterations to the travelling party as the "most shocking decision ever by a selection committee".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pakistan's Saud Shakeel missed out on a Lord's century, holing out off Josh Tongue to fall for 97 against England in the second Test

Of the seven replacements who have been called up, only batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have Test experience.

The PCB's statement on Monday added: "The PCB will not comment further at this time. The board advises stakeholders and the public to rely on official PCB communications."

New Pakistan coaches in the dark over investigation

Noffke addressed the media in Birmingham on Monday, admitting he was unaware of the specifics of the probe.

"I can be really honest in that I don't know too much," he said. "I sit outside of that decision-making model, (which is) above us as coaches. We try and keep the players focused on what they need to worry about.

"One thing that I've learned about being in Pakistan and coaching for a period of time, nearly 15 months now with the white-ball team, is there's always something going on in the background.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at some funny moments from the England vs Pakistan Test series!

"I think most of the time it's out of the players' control. They need to focus on the cricket that they have in front of them and the opportunity they have in front of them.

"We're not really in the position to even know the outer workings of what's happening at PCB in that context."

Noffke also admitted that taking over mid-series as part of head coach Hesson's staff was "unusual".

He added: "It doesn't happen very often and I guess from Mike and my perspective is all we can do is come in and add positivity.

"We want to listen to the players as much as we can, so there's obviously a feeling of uncertainty but also they've just got back on the job."
