Ravi Ravichandran, President of Ford Middle East and North Africa, stated that Iraq remains a central growth market for the company’s regional strategy, noting that SAT’s combination of local commercial expertise and dealership infrastructure will support customer engagement through the purchase and ownership cycle.

World.title: Resolution doesn't endorse any specific map: MEA
World.content:
India was among the 164 countries that voted in favour of UN General Assembly's Sept 4 resolution, "Correct the Map: Rebalancing Global Cartographic Representation and Promoting Equitable Representation of the World's Regions, Particularly Africa".

MEA said the resolution's purpose is to encourage the use of equal-area map projections that preserve the relative sizes of continental landmasses, and it neither adopts nor authenticates any particular world map, nor does it address political cartography, including international boundaries, disputed territories or place names.

"India voted in favour of the resolution and also made an explanation, stressing the underlying principle of promoting equal-area cartographic representation.

We also highlighted that the resolution does not constitute endorsement of any specific map, projection or depiction of national boundaries," said Randhir Jaiswal.

The resolution received abstentions from Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine, and a lone vote against it from US.

World.title: Company can be punished for offence carrying imprisonment, term can be replaced by fine: Supreme Court
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A company having no physical body cannot be imprisoned and having no mind cannot possess mens rea (guilty mind), which is essential for conviction in a criminal case. So can a firm be convicted and punished?SC Monday answered the tricky questions by holding that a company can be convicted even when it cannot have a guilty mind of its own and can also be punished, though the punishment of a jail term can be substituted by a fine.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Manoj Misra said there is a need to bring a law for corporate criminal liability but said the issue comes within the legislature's prerogative and it cannot be done by a court. It held that a company is not rendered immune to prosecution merely because the offence carries a mandatory sentence of imprisonment. Referring to a constitution bench ruling, the bench said a judicial discretion to impose a fine alone must be read into such provisions when dealing with juristic persons."The position under Indian law is thus clear that a corporation can be prosecuted for an offence notwithstanding that it carries a mandatory sentence of imprisonment or requires proof of mens rea. It appears that a corporation cannot be prosecuted only where the offence is punishable with imprisonment alone, or where the offence, by its nature, requires personal malicious intent, such that it is incapable of commission by a corporation at all," the bench said.SC passed the order on a plea by Sanofi India Ltd which said a prosecution against a corporation like it, for an offence requiring mens rea, is maintainable only where a natural person has been identified and arraigned as an accused alongside it. It said that corporations alone cannot be convicted and pleaded that proceedings against it should be quashed. Rejecting the plea of the company, the bench said non-identification of the natural person does not, by itself, render the allegations incapable of disclosing the corporation's role in the offence.The case pertains to the supply of pharmaceutical products by Sanofi India to Bhabha Atomic Research Centre. As per CBI, a BARC officer had conspired with the company to procure medicines at inflated prices and in quantities exceeding the requirement. A case was registered against Sanofi, which challenged its prosecution on the ground that none of its employees had been made accused and a company alone cannot be prosecuted."... where the surrounding facts and circumstances, taken as a whole, disclose the possibility that the corporation acted with the requisite mens rea, that disclosure is not defeated merely because no particular individual has been identified as its source. Therefore, the ingredient of mens rea can still be disclosed even where no individual has been identified," the bench said while rejecting the plea of the company.

World.title: Passive smoking deaths up 50% since 1990: Lancet
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Deaths linked to second-hand smoke in India have soared, surging almost 50% since 1990 and claiming 325,600 lives in 2023 alone. According to a study published in The Lancet Public Health Monday, India had the world's second-highest number of people exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, after China, with 444 million Indians affected.

While India's age-standardised exposure prevalence declined from 43.2% to 30.6% over the last three decades, the absolute number of people exposed rose from 375 million in 1990 to 444 million in 2023, an increase of 18.4%. The health toll also rose sharply, with deaths attributable to second-hand smoke climbing from 217,700 to 325,600 during the same period.

Fatalities among women rose from 113,400 to 156,900, while deaths among men from 104,300 to 168,700 over the same period.

Second-hand smoke also accounted for 9.28 million disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in India in 2023, representing healthy years lost to premature death, illness or disability.

Dr G C Khilnani, chairperson of pulmonary, critical care at PSRI Hospital, said, "Second-hand smoke contributes not only to illness and disability but also to premature deaths and loss of healthy years. Kids and women are particularly vulnerable, with children's developing lungs making them more susceptible to respiratory issues.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





Smoking should be done outdoors, and greater public awareness is needed."

The study links second-hand smoke to ischaemic heart disease, stroke, lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, breast cancer, type 2 diabetes, asthma and lower respiratory infections. Among children, lower respiratory infections were the leading contributor to the disease burden.

Globally, 2.71 billion people were exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, contributing to 1.66 million deaths and 44.8 million DALYs. China, India and Indonesia accounted for nearly half of world's exposed population, with China recording 664 million exposed people.

World.title: Rural area LPG booking period reduced from 45 to 25 days
World.content:
Rural area LPG booking period reduced from 45 to 25 days

NEW DELHI: With improvement in LPG supplies and a fall in refill backlogs, govt Monday reduced the minimum time gap for booking LPG refills in rural areas to 25 days from 45 days, bringing it on a par with the interval for urban consumers, reports Atul Mathur.Union minister of state for petroleum and natural gas Suresh Gopi said the restriction had been imposed amid pressure on LPG supplies following the outbreak of the conflict in West Asia, with the booking interval set at 25 days in urban areas and 45 days in rural areas."However, in view of the current LPG supply situation improving and the significant reduction in refill backlog, Centre has relaxed this restriction. Now, all domestic LPG consumers, regardless of urban or rural, can book refills at an interval of 25 days," Gopi said. Petroleum ministry has issued an order to oil marketing companies IOC, BPCL and HPCL, asking them to implement this with immediate effect.

World.content:

âThe details of how Aqib Bashir escaped from custody are unclear... Police and other security agencies have intensified frisking and vehicle checks at key entry and exit points across the region,â an official said.

Bashir, from Pulwama districtâs Kakapora, was arrested with 522 grams of heroin on Sept 3, when an NCB team intercepted a Jammu-bound bus coming from Punjab at new bus stand in Samba. NCB in its statement on Sept 5 claimed to have exposed a twin-route narco-trail in J&K: one originating from across the Pakistan border and another operating through PunjabâJ&K corridor.

World.title: U.K. recognises India's carbon credit scheme under its carbon tax mechanism: official
World.content:
In a major breakthrough, the U.K. has recognised India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme as a qualifying criterion for pricing relief under its carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM), a move that would reduce the tax burden on domestic exporters, an official said on Monday (September 7, 2026).

In a communication addressed to the Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Ministry of Power, the U.K.'s HM Treasury confirmed that the CCTS has been included in the U.K.'s published indicative list of overseas carbon pricing schemes assessed as qualifying criteria under a provision of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (Calculation of CBAM Rate and Determination of Carbon Price Relief) Regulations 2026, the official said.

The move is important as the Commerce Ministry was pursuing the matter with the U.K. for long.

The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) has been notified by India with the objective of reducing, removing, or avoiding greenhouse gas emissions from the Indian economy by pricing such emissions through the trading of Carbon Credit Certificates.

The financial support for implementation of the CCTS would be met by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency from fees and charges collected from entities under the scheme and its own resources.

The official said the U.K. government had included the scheme in its indicative list as a qualifying carbon pricing mechanism under Britain's CBAM.

With this recognition, U.K. importers of eligible Indian goods covered under CBAM will be able to seek carbon price relief corresponding to the effective carbon price borne by those goods under the CCTS, subject to satisfying the evidence and verification requirements prescribed under U.K. law.

"This will reduce the effective CBAM liability on Indian goods, directly benefiting Indian exporters to the U.K.," the official said.

The recognition follows sustained technical-level engagement between the two governments on the design and implementation of the CCTS.

The recognition reflects the U.K. CBAM's core principle of avoiding double taxation on goods that have already borne an eligible carbon price in their country of origin.

Going forward, cooperation on carbon market design and implementation will continue through the U.K.-India Energy Memorandum of Understanding and the Partnership for Market Implementation.

The two governments are also committed to continued dialogue on carbon pricing, including on the interaction between the CCTS and U.K. CBAM rules, further strengthening India-U.K. engagement.

However, the amount of relief that can be claimed will depend on the effective carbon price to which the goods in question have been subject.

A liable person for U.K. CBAM will still be required to satisfy the applicable evidence and verification requirements.

India and the U.K. have implemented a comprehensive economic and trade partnership on July 15.

Merchandise trade between the two countries stood at $25.1 billion in 2025-26, while bilateral services trade reached $35.4 billion in 2024.

World.title: West Asia conflict updates: Iran warns U.S. energy assets in Gulf are vulnerable after latest clashes
World.content:
Iran threatened on Monday (September 7, 2026) to retaliate against any new U.S. attacks on its assets, warning that energy infrastructure across the Gulf, including U.S. oil and ‌gas interests, was vulnerable. “Strike our assets and you get struck,” Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said after U.S. and Iranian strikes on shipping at the weekend that pushed oil prices up near six-week highs on Monday (September 7).

Israeli strikes on a southern Lebanese town early on Monday (September 7, 2026) killed at least 11 people including two children and two medics, ‌Lebanon’s state news agency said.

Israel has intensified its bombardment of south Lebanon in recent days ⁠despite a June ceasefire that was meant to halt fighting between the Israeli military and Lebanese armed group Hezbollah. At ‌least seven people were killed in Israeli strikes on Sunday.

The Israeli army demanded early Monday that residents of Deir Zahrani in southern Lebanon leave a specific zone ahead of strikes against Iran-backed Hezbollah.

(With inputs from agencies)

World.title: Paris investigates claim of women being removed during Hindu delegation visit at Eiffel Tower
World.content:
Female employees at the Eiffel Tower were ​asked to step out of sight during a visit by a ‌Hindu religious delegation at the weekend, according to union representatives, prompting ​a staff protest and an investigation by Paris city ⁠authorities.

The monument was closed late on Monday (September 7, 2026) as employees held a meeting over the incident, which has angered staff and drawn criticism from French politicians.

On Saturday, ‌a delegation of about 100 people linked to the Hindu group Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, or BAPS, made ‌a private visit to the Eiffel Tower.

“As the delegation ‌passed ⁠through, women were asked to leave their workstations so that ⁠men could take their places,” Diane Davoine, a union representative, told Reuters.

“Tensions mounted over the weekend, so this morning, the employees decided to meet: first, to open ​a dialogue with management, and second, ‌to ensure that women are never treated this way at the company again,” she said.

Signs at the base of the tower on Monday read: “The opening of the Eiffel Tower is delayed for ‌operational reasons.”

Ms. Davoine said management apologised to staff over the incident.

Paris ​Mayor reacts to the incident

Paris ​Mayor Emmanuel Gregoire said that an investigation would be launched “as soon as possible”. In a post on social media ⁠platform X, he said he was aware of the employees’ anger and agreed their dissatisfaction was legitimate.

“It is urgent that all light ‌be shed on the facts that led to this protest,” Mr. Gregoire wrote.

BAPS, whose representatives were in France for festivities related to the inauguration of a Hindu temple in the Paris suburbs, said in a statement that the visit to the Eiffel Tower was arranged at the start of opening hours to avoid disrupting others, due to ‌the size of its delegation.

“To the best of our knowledge, at no point ​was anyone prevented access to the Eiffel Tower. Nevertheless, we sincerely apologise for any pain or inconvenience caused,” the ⁠statement said.

A spokesperson for SETE, the company operating the monument, did not immediately ⁠respond to a request for comment.

Yael Braun-Pivet, the president of the National Assembly, wrote in a post on X: “Welcoming ‌others never means giving up our values. In France, women are fully present in public life. No one tells them to become ​invisible.”

World.title: Delhi’s student hubs: soaring rents, ageing buildings and little room to breathe
World.content:
The collapse of a five-storey building housing students in Satya Niketan on Sunday has brought renewed scrutiny to the cramped living spaces and the compromises students make in the absence of affordable hostel accommodation.

In Delhi’s student hubs, narrow lanes, ageing buildings pressed against each other, dangling electricity and cable wires, and rooms carved out wherever space permits have become a familiar reality. For thousands of outstation students arriving in the Capital each year, these converted houses and tightly packed buildings are often the only affordable options, with a bed in a shared room costing anywhere from ₹12,000 to over ₹24,000 a month.

Near Delhi University’s (DU) South Campus, Satya Niketan is a maze of small shops, property dealers, old buildings and newer constructions connected by uneven roads.

Unnayan, who moved to Delhi last month, lives about 100 metres from the collapsed building. He paid ₹14,000 this month, including the security deposit, for a bed on the fifth floor, where he no longer wants to live.

“I chose the fifth floor and have to go up and down the stairs because the lower floors were more expensive. A bed on the second floor cost ₹17,000, and the first floor was even more expensive,” he said.

Common theme

At the other end of the city, in Jawahar Nagar near DU’s North Campus, a narrow lane is choked with parked vehicles on both sides, leaving little room for pedestrians. Small shops are wedged between residential buildings, while a web of electricity and cable wires hangs overhead.

Rakhi, a native of Haryana and a first-year Bcom student at Daulat Ram College, pointed to a ground-plus-five-storey building where she has been living for a month.

“I pay ₹17,000 for a bed and food, which is pathetic. Electricity is an additional cost,” she said.

With no hostel available, Rakhi began looking for a paying guest (PG) accommodation when the academic session started. Her first room, on a lower floor, cost ₹14,000 for double-sharing but was, she said, “not liveable at all”.

“The rooms are very cramped. There is barely any ventilation. The rent is too high, but at least this is a room I can somehow survive in,” she said.

A 10-minute scooter ride away, Nehru Nagar appears to narrow further with every turn. Buildings rise to five floors, their tiny entrances leading to uneven staircases and corridors punctuated by air conditioners jutting out from walls.

Riddhima (name changed on request), a final-year DU student, has spent four years in one such PG.

“The place is not ideal to live in, with no ventilation or space even to walk, but this was the best I could find,” she said. Other PGs nearby offer essentially the same arrangement, a bed in a shared room, for ₹17,000 to ₹20,000.

Less than a kilometre away, Kamla Nagar is another student hub where almost every other building houses a PG.

Tanya, a second-year DU student, pays ₹12,000 for a bed in a double-sharing room. The room has no window or ventilator, forcing her to keep the air conditioner running to make it bearable.

“Otherwise, it gets very suffocating,” she said.

Across Delhi’s student colonies, space has become a premium that students are paying dearly for, even when it amounts to little more than a bed squeezed into an ageing building.

World.title: Sealing drive imminent, PG at Satya Niketan asks all 40 female occupants to move out
World.content:
A women’s PG facility in Satya Niketan, located 300 metres from the five-storey structure that collapsed the previous day, on Monday asked all occupants to vacate their rooms immediately.

‘Sealing imminent’

A student said they were told that the hostel could be sealed any time and that the facility would operate only as long as supplies last.

Of the estimated 40 occupants, only 22 currently remain in the facility. The rest left for their hometowns soon after the incident, said a student.

“My parents just left after helping me with the admission and lodging. They are now worried and want to take me away. But it will take them two days to arrive by train. What will I do until then?” said Himanshi Aggarwal, who hails from Assam.

Air of uncertainty

Thousands of outstation students who paid rent and security deposits in advance at PG facilities in the south-west Delhi locality are facing uncertainty after Sunday’s incident, with the authorities announcing a sealing drive against unauthorised structures.

‘University apathetic’

“The college is still open. The administration has not shown any interest in understanding our situation. How will we attend classes if we go back to our hometowns?” added Ms. Aggarwal, a Maitreyi College student.

Prajakta, a first-year student, said, “We have not been given an exact date. The warden has only asked us to vacate rooms as soon as possible”.

‘Paid security, rent’

“I rented a ₹16,000 twin-occupancy room. I paid two months’ rent as a security deposit and the current month’s rent in advance. In all, I have already paid ₹48,000,” added Ms. Prajakta.

The women’s PG, which shares the name ‘Hostel Daze’ with the facility in the collapsed building, is also located in a five-storey structure.

There are four rooms on each floor except the ground floor, which has three. For now, students have packed their essential belongings and made arrangements to stay with friends or relatives.

World.title: Sanjay Kumar Agrawal sworn in as Rajasthan HC Chief Justice
World.content:
Justice Sanjay Kumar Agrawal, transferred from Chhattisgarh, was sworn in as the 44th Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court at a ceremony held at Lok Bhavan here on Monday (September 7, 2026). Governor Haribhau Bagade administered the oath of office in the presence of Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma, his Cabinet colleagues, judges and administrative officials.

The Union government notified Justice Agrawal’s elevation as the Chief Justice and appointment in Rajasthan following a recommendation by the Supreme Court Collegium. He was first appointed as an additional judge of the Chhattisgarh High Court in September 2013 and became a permanent judge in March 2016.

Justice Agrawal left for Jodhpur immediately after the swearing-in ceremony for joining the judicial work at the High Court’s principal seat. His appointment is considered significant for streamlining the judicial system in the State and ensuring speedy disposal of the pending cases.

Justice Agrawal’s appointment in Rajasthan comes amid a controversy surrounding Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma, who had been serving as the High Court’s Acting Chief Justice since September 2025. A Supreme Court judge, Justice Sandeep Mehta, recently wrote a series of letters to the Chief Justice of India making complaints about Justice Sharma’s conduct and seeking his transfer.

Justice Mehta alleged “misuse of powers, favouritism, nepotism, and administrative lapses” by Justice Sharma in his letters. The issue also triggered protests by lawyers in Jodhpur as well as at the High Court’s Bench in Jaipur. The protesting lawyers demanded that Justice Sharma be divested of his charge and a permanent Chief Justice be appointed in the State.

Justice Sharma, who is due to retire on September 26, has rejected the allegations levelled against him as baseless and called upon all concerned to “remain patient” until the CJI takes a decision. In a statement released last week, Justice Sharma said he had placed his version with the supporting evidence before the CJI.

World.title: Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai, others detained as row over Saharanpur mosque demolition escalates
World.content:
Uttar Pradesh Police on Monday (September 7, 2026) detained senior state Congress leaders including State Congress President Ajay Rai in Lucknow after they attempted to visit Saharanpur over the demolition of a historic mosque within the Saharanpur Collectorate complex.

The Congress described the police action as dictatorship, adding the administration is working on the directions of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government to silence the voices of opposition. Mr. Rai and other Congress leaders were released in the evening after hours of detention.

“Following the brutal action of bulldozing the historic mosque located in the Saharanpur Collectorate premises, I along with other party leaders were going to take stock of the situation there today, but we were forcibly detained by the police as soon as he left the Lucknow party office. This authoritarian action is clear evidence that the BJP government is deeply afraid of the Congress party’s democratic pushback. This repressive and undemocratic approach by the administration will not be able to suppress the Congress’s high spirits and strong resolve. It is struggle against injustice and dictatorship. Along with us, hundreds of other brave party leaders and workers also stood firm in this protest. The Congress Party will continue to vigorously oppose every excess committed by this government, which has murdered democracy and the Constitution,” told Mr. Rai, to The Hindu.

A Samajwadi Party (SP) delegation consisting of some MPs and other party leaders submitted a petition to the authorities in Saharanpur addressed to the President of India seeking action on officers responsible for demolition. “Today, as per the instructions of respected National President Shri Akhilesh Yadav ji, a memorandum was submitted to the Additional Commissioner regarding the demolition of a 119-year-old mosque in Saharanpur.

The judicial process must be followed in this entire matter, and action must be taken in accordance with the Constitution. I also appeal to maintain mutual brotherhood, harmony, and peace in society. There is an emergency-like situation in this government; the commissioner was not available even after giving time,” said Harendra Malik, a SP Lok Sabha MP.

In a related development, an Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) team on Monday examined a well discovered during debris removal at the site of the demolished mosque on the premises of the Saharanpur collectorate, officials said. ASI officials reached the site in afternoon and examined the well in the presence of local administration officials, Sadar Sub-Divisional Magistrate Subodh Kumar said.

“The ASI officials measured the depth of the well after placing a ladder inside and examined its interior. They also carried out photography and videography and collected samples of soil and brick remnants from inside the well as part of their investigation,” said the SDM, to local reporters.

World.title: Eknath Shinde suspends Sena leader arrested over attack on medical staff
World.content:
Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister and Shiv Sena chief Eknath Shinde on Monday (September 7, 2026) suspended the party’s Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat following the latter’s arrest over the alleged assault on employees of a private hospital by Shiv Sena workers a day ago. Mr. Shinde said such incidents would not be tolerated and warned of strict action against anyone found responsible.

Inspector Kishor Mahanubhav of the Palghar police station said Mr. Gharat was produced before a local magistrate, who remanded him to police custody for a day.

This is the second such incident of assault by Sena leader in the recent past. Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre was arrested for allegedly assaulting doctors at a Thane hospital on July 6.

A wider probe into the Palghar attack was under way even as the police remain on the lookout for the remaining accused persons, the officer said.

According to the police, five ‘govindas’ who were a part of a Shiv Sena Dahi Handi celebrations in Palghar were admitted to Relief Hospital in Palghar.

“The bill for the treatment of the govindas came to ₹19,000. Seventeen Sena members came to the hospital and had already paid ₹10,000; the remaining amount was yet to be paid. One of the ‘govindas’, aged 19, wanted to go home in Virar. But the doctor said he wanted to keep him for 24-hour observation,” Mr. Mahanubhav said. The officer added that the party members refused to pay the remaining amount until the 19-year-old was released, following which an argument broke out and the party workers assaulted the staff.

CCTV footage

Mr. Gharat, who was part of the group, allegedly slapped a staff member. CCTV footage from the hospital purportedly shows one person slapping a receptionist. The police have registered an FIR against 17 individuals.

World.title: Govt jacks up petrol price by Rs12.90, HSD by Rs3.72
World.content:
The government on Monday jacked up the price of petrol by Rs12.90 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.72 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs358.77 per litre while HSD will cost Rs381.77 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 8 (Tuesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Senate panel passes bill proposing death penalty for perpetrators of acid attacks
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Senate Standing Committee on Interior on Monday passed a series of key criminal law amendments, including a bill proposing the death penalty for acid attacks, as it moved to strengthen protections for vulnerable groups and public safety.

Chaired by Senator Faisal Saleem Rehman, the committee considered private members’ bills relating to acid crimes, protection of domestic workers, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) safety, anti-rape legislation and consumer protection.

The bills were passed despite opposition from State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, with PPP lawmakers also voting in favour.

The Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill moved by Senator Muhammad Abdul Qadir, seeking to amend Section 336B of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) relating to hurt caused by corrosive substances, was passed in the absence of the mover.

Citing “the recent incident of acid attack on a lady doctor in Quetta”, the bill states that despite the 2011 amendment, acid attacks continue to cause lifelong disfigurement and trauma.

It proposes the punishment of “death or imprisonment for life or imprisonment of not less than 14 years and a fine of Rs2 million” to serve as a strong deterrent.

The committee also unanimously passed the Criminal Laws (Amendment) Bill moved by Senator Sarmad Ali, proposing to criminalise the abuse of domestic workers.

The Statement of Objects and Reasons notes that “domestic workers constitute one of the most vulnerable segments of society, often subjected to physical violence, sexual abuse, forced labour, and other forms of mistreatment by employers.”

It adds that “existing provisions… do not specifically address the abuse arising from dependency and control inherent in domestic work settings”.

The proposed section covers physical violence, sexual harassment, threats, forced labour, wage theft, confiscation of identity documents, denial of food or medical care, and humiliating treatment.

The proposed penalties are “imprisonment for a term which may extend to 10 years and fine which may extend to Rs100,000” and “imprisonment for life and fine which may extend to Rs500,000” if the offence causes serious injury or death.

The bill also makes employers liable if abuse is committed by household members, “unless the employer took reasonable steps to prevent such abuse”.

Schedule II of the Criminal Procedure Code has also been amended to make the offence non-bailable and triable by a court of session.

In a move to address public safety hazards, the committee passed the Criminal Laws (Amendment) Act, moved by Senator Shahadat Awan, to amend Sections 286 and 286A of the PPC to criminalise the unauthorised transfer of LPG into smaller cylinders.

Noting that such decanting in residential areas and roadside setups poses severe risks, the bill increases the punishment under Section 286 from six months to two years and the fine from Rs1,000 to Rs100,000. Under Section 286A, imprisonment is increased from two to five years and the fine from Rs10,000 to Rs500,000.

The Statement of Objects and Reasons notes that “the decanting of LPG from larger cylinders into smaller domestic cylinders without proper safety measures has become a widespread practice in many parts of Pakistan.” It adds that “these unauthorised decanting operations are often conducted in residential areas, workshops, or roadside setups without adherence to safety standards, posing severe risks to public life and property.”

The bill proposes raising the punishment under Section 286 from six months to two years and the fine from Rs1,000 to Rs100,000. Under Section 286A, it proposes increasing the term of imprisonment from two to five years and the fine from Rs10,000 to Rs500,000.

“The proposed amendments aim to deter negligent and reckless conduct in the handling of explosive and hazardous substances, ensuring greater public safety and accountability.”

The committee also unanimously passed the Criminal Laws (Amendment) Bill, moved by Senator Samina Mumtaz Zehri, proposing to insert a new Section 338CA to make “Wrongful Detention of Dead Body” a punishable offence.

The Statement of Objects and Reasons highlights that “there have been numerous reports of private hospitals and clinics detaining the dead bodies of patients until their families settle outstanding medical bills”.

It cites examples of hospitals that “demand exorbitant advance deposits, sometimes as high as Rs2m to Rs4m” and “withhold dead bodies even when outstanding dues are as low as Rs100,000.”

The statement argues that this “not only causes immense psychological harm to grieving families but also denies the deceased the right to timely burial and dignified last rites, which is a fundamental religious obligation in Islam and other religions.” It adds that “the inviolability of human dignity does not cease upon death.”

The new section proposes a punishment of up to two years’ imprisonment and/or a fine of Rs500,000 for a first offence, and up to three years’ imprisonment and/or a fine of Rs1m for a second offence or detention beyond 24 hours. Exceptions are provided for autopsies or police investigations. The offence has been made compoundable by the legal heirs.

The Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) (Amendment) Bill, moved by Bushra Anjum Butt, was also passed, with the committee observing that legislation aimed at strengthening the legal framework against rape should receive appropriate government support.

On the consumer side, the committee passed the Islamabad Consumers Protection (Amendment) Bill, also moved by Senator Zehri, to bring private healthcare under the 1995 Act. The bill targets undisclosed fees, non-itemised billing and demands for advance deposits before emergency treatment, and requires hospitals to publicly display fee schedules and provide itemised bills.

The committee expressed serious concern over reports that former parliamentarians were being required to obtain a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the Ministry of Interior for the issuance of official passports and that their validity had been reduced from five years to one year. The minister of state for interior said only the internal approval procedure had been changed.

The chairman directed that existing law must not be violated and that official passports be issued with five-year validity in accordance with the law. Further deliberation was deferred.

The Ministry of Interior also briefed the committee on concerns regarding the unregulated use of social media by minors, stating that a high-powered committee was working on proposals to regulate its use by children.

Last week, a 35-year-old woman suffered burns when a man threw acid on her in Karachi’s Upper Gizri area.

Earlier in June, 29-year-old Mahnoor Nasir was seriously injured at the Quetta Civil Hospital when another employee threw acid on her. The attacker, later identified by police as Humayun Shah, was said to have been kil­led in an encounter after law enforcers tra­ced him as he attempted to flee on a bus.

Meanwhile, Dr Nasir was shifted to Karachi after receiving initial treatment in Quetta.

World.title: Pakistan through to Women’s Asia Cup semi-finals as Nashra leads Hong Kong rout
World.content:
Pakistan booked their place in the Women’s Asia Cup semi-finals after spinner Nashra Sandhu’s triggered a 72-run drubbing of Hong Kong, China at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Monday night.

Nashra took six wickets as Pakistan defended 143 runs — that included a stand-out contribution by Shawaal Zulfiqaar — to set their last-four date against Sri Lanka on Friday.

Pakistan skipper Fatima Sana, for the third match in a row, chose to bat first, looking to undo the damage of Pakistan’s hefty seven-wicket loss against India at the same venue on Saturday, where they were bowled out for their lowest ever T20 international score.

The teams were unchanged from their previous matches, both of which came against India.

Pakistan once again got off to a steady start with the bat, with openers Muneeba Ali and Shawaal easing their way to a 24-run opening partnership in three overs until Muneeba, who was too early on a shot, was bowled by Iqra Sahar.

Gull Feroza at number three continued her unconvincing run in the tournament as she was dismissed leg-before-wicket on three off four balls after two consecutive ducks in the previous matches.

Ayesha Zafar got off to a swift start with back-to-back boundaries when she came out to bat at number four to join Shawaal at the crease.

Shawaal played perhaps the most convincing knock coming from a Pakistan batter this tournament, constructing a discerning yet well-paced knock of 47 off 35 balls, rotating strike and sending the odd ball away to ensure Pakistan could launch off a stable base.

Ayesha Zafar fell after a handy knock of 26 off 19 balls, mistiming Joyleen’s Kaur slower tossed-up delivery, and unable to get it through the in-field. The wicket meant Pakistan were 82-3 at the halfway mark of their batting innings.

Pakistan once again suffered from a middle-overs wobble as Shawaal, Sadaf Shamas and Eyman Fatima lost their wickets — all of them to Kaur — within the space of nine runs, with the team suddenly finding themselves at a shaky 101-6.

Fatima (run-a-ball 24 not out) calmed Pakistan’s jitters, taking the team to 127 along with Tuba Hassan (14 off 13), who hit a four and a six off Kary Chan’s bowling before muddling an attempt to come down the track and getting bowled by her.

Though the last two overs were quiet, coupled with the wicket of Umm-e-Hani, a six off the penultimate ball by the captain meant Pakistan ended their innings at 143-8, an above par total on a tricky pitch.

Disciplined start

Pakistan got off to a splendid start with the ball, with Fatima and Sadia Iqbal striking in consecutive overs, leaving Hong Kong at 1-2 at the two-over mark.

Fatima bowled Mariko Hill off the last ball of the first over, ending a run-less Asia Cup campaign for the batter, while Sadia pinned Miles lbw off her first ball.

Yasmin Daswani and Kary Chan fought well, putting together a 31-run partnership off 44 balls and ensuring Pakistan’s moments of indiscipline with the ball were punished.

Nashra’s spectacular evening

The introduction of Nashra, however, was not just decisive for Pakistan, but all-crushing for Hong Kong.

She caught and bowled Daswani for the third wicket, breaking Hong Kong’s resistance and then single-handedly opened the floodgates. She dismissed Marina Lamplough soon after, before tempting Bibi to play across the line — which she did, ultimately getting caught by Sadaf at midwicket.

Shanzeen Shahzad did the same, caught by Sadia at extra-cover, and Alison Siu was bowled on the very next ball, with Nashra securing her maiden T20I five-wicket haul.

She soon became the first Pakistani to get a six-wicket haul in T20 internationals, as she bowled Sahar off the last ball of her four-over spell, finishing on stellar figures of 6-7.

With Nashra having ripped through the line-up, Hong Kong eventually were bowled out for 71 runs, their innings extended only because of missed chances in the field by Pakistan. Umm-e-Hani took the final wicket of Joyleen Kaur to secure the 72-run win for Pakistan. Nashra was unsurprisingly named player of the match.

With this result, Hong Kong, who needed to chase the total in 12.3 overs to qualify for the semi-finals were knocked out, while Pakistan secured a spot in the final four.

World.title: JI submits six proposals as first round of talks with govt concludes
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The first round of talks between Jamaat-i-Islami and the federal government on abolishing the petroleum levy and providing relief to the public concluded in Islamabad on Monday, with the party submitting six key proposals to the government committee.

Both sides agreed to hold the next round on Thursday.

Last week, the government and JI agreed to form committees comprising experts to discuss recommendations for reducing the petroleum levy and providing relief to the public.

The JI delegation was led by Vice Emir Liaqat Baloch and comprised Deputy Secretary Syed Farasat Shah, KP Emir Inayatullah Khan, Lahore Emir Advocate Ziaur Rehman Ansari, Islamabad Emir Nasrullah Randhawa, Naveed Ali Baig and Shahid Naeem.

Meanwhile, the government side was headed by Federal Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and included Prime Minister’s Adviser Rana Sanaullah, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and State Minister for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani.

Addressing the media after the meeting on Monday, Baloch said they had presented six detailed proposals to the prime minister’s team, emphasising that the “direct Rs80 petroleum levy per litre on petrol and diesel is severely impacting the national economy”.

He clarified that peaceful sit-ins and protests across the country would continue while negotiations proceeded.

“The primary objective remains providing immediate relief to the public,” Baloch added, urging rulers to cut state expenditures as sufficient budgetary margin exists to accommodate tax relief.

Baloch also expressed concern over unfulfilled government commitments made during previous talks regarding independent power producers (IPPs), adding that daily petroleum pricing should be discontinued.

He also noted that the current subsidy structures had failed to deliver and provide relief to the public.

Baloch said it was encouraging that the government had always given priority to negotiations. He reiterated that dialogue was the only solution and said JI also understood that protests were not a solution.

However, he told the government that public frustration was increasing due to rising electricity, gas and petrol prices.

The party leader further said, “We know that we are caught in the IMF’s grip and that many decisions are being taken by the government out of compulsion.”

Addressing the media, Iqbal said that the government had invited JI for talks to seek its actionable suggestions, which had now been formally received.

The minister added that the meeting had been convened to review JI’s proposals regarding the petroleum levy in detail, adding that there were certain national economic realities that could not be denied.

He noted that the relevant government institutions would review the recommendations and that any impractical points would be discussed openly with JI during the upcoming session.

The planning minister said the government never wanted to overburden citizens, but global economies had been disrupted by regional tensions, including the US-Israeli war on Iran.

“Petroleum prices would naturally ease once regional conflicts de-escalate,” he added.

He stressed that the government and all stakeholders were concerned about the public interest and that the government did not want to impose any additional burden on the people.

“If any relief can be provided to the people in any way, we will be very happy ourselves,” he said.

Responding to a question about the policy rate, he said the government did not determine it, as the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) was autonomous in this regard. He added that the SBP’s policy board decided the policy rate after taking inflation into account.

Iqbal also announced the next course of action, saying JI’s proposals concerned various ministries and that the views of the relevant institutions would be sought on them.

He said a second round of talks would be held within three days after feedback was received from the relevant institutions.

World.title: Interpol Pakistan issues 286 red notices in 7 months, 53 fugitives repatriated
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Interpol’s National Central Bureau (NCB) in Pakistan issued 286 Red Notices in the last seven months as part of efforts to track fugitives involved in murder, fraud, terrorism and human trafficking, according to Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) Director General Dr Usman Anwar.

A Red Notice is a request to law enforcement agencies by Interpol to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition, surrender or similar legal action.

Anwar, who also heads NCB-Interpol Pakistan, reaffirmed the agency’s resolve on World Day of International Police Cooperation, adding that Islamabad would continue to strengthen collaboration with Interpol and global partners.

NCBs serve as each country’s focal point for all Interpol activities. They connect national law enforcement agencies with those in other countries and with the Interpol General Secretariat through a secure global police communications network known as I-24/7, allowing real-time access to databases and services.

Anwar said NCB-Interpol Pakistan issued a total of 290 Interpol notices during the period, including two Blue Notices and two Yellow Notices.

Yellow Notices are meant to help locate missing persons, often minors, or identify people who are unable to identify themselves, while Blue Notices are issued to collect additional information.

Of the 286 Red Notices, 225 were issued for suspects wanted in murder and attempted murder cases, while another 33 were issued for individuals wanted in kidnapping, corruption, robbery and cybercrime cases.

The bureau also issued 19 Red Notices for financial fraud and deception, six for human trafficking and three for terrorism.

Through international cooperation, 53 fugitives wanted in Pakistan for serious crimes were arrested in different countries and extradited to Pakistan during the same seven-month period.

“Today’s crimes are increasingly international. Cybercrime, fugitives and stolen goods driven by organised groups — none of these respect borders,” Anwar told Dawn.

“We seek information from other NCBs to help investigations in Pakistan, and we share our criminal data to assist other countries.”

He added that NCBs were critical because they could trigger law enforcement action in their respective countries and work directly with counterparts, even between states without diplomatic relations.

“When a crime goes beyond our national jurisdiction, we need international support to solve it. Interpol provides that platform,” he stated.

According to Interpol’s framework, NCBs contribute national crime data to global databases in accordance with national laws. Red Notices, for example, alert police in all 196 member countries to wanted persons.

NCB Pakistan works with domestic law enforcement agencies, other NCBs and sub-bureaus worldwide, as well as the General Secretariat’s offices, to coordinate cross-border investigations, operations and arrests. The FIA director general noted that regional cooperation was growing as countries combined resources to tackle shared threats.

“We are also building capacity at home. NCBs develop training programmes for national police to raise awareness of Interpol’s tools and databases so that our officers can use them effectively on the ground,” Anwar said.

“FIA NCB-Interpol Pakistan remains committed to ensuring that no fugitive finds safe haven abroad. Through I-24/7 and our network of partners, we will keep pursuing criminals and bringing them to justice.”

In April this year, Interpol issued Red Notices against Bahria Town owner Malik Riaz and his son Ali Riaz, Nat­i­onal Accountability Bur­eau (NAB) Chairman Lt General (retired) Nazir Ahmed said.

Last month, the National Cybercrime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) arrested two suspects and initiated the process for obtaining Red Notices for the remaining four alleged members of the “Tycoon2FA Cybercrime Network”.

World.title: Karachi police briefly detain protesting family members of Pakistani sailors held hostage by Somali pirates
World.content:
KARACHI: Some family members of Pakistani sailors, who have been held hostage by Somali pirates aboard the MT Honour 25 for more than four months, were briefly detained on Monday morning while they were staging a sit-in at Karachi’s Sharea Faisal.

The MT Honour 25, a Palau-flagged oil tanker, was hijacked by armed pirates off the coast of Puntland, Somalia, on April 21. Besides 10 crew members from Pakistan, the hostages include seamen from Indonesia, India and Sri Lanka.

During more than four months of their captivity, no significant progress has been reported either in negotiations or in the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for their recovery.

Their families have staged protests for their recovery multiple times.

On Sunday, they began an overnight sit-in at Sharea Faisal outside the Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ (Mofa) liaison office and planned to march to the Supreme Court registry on Monday morning. But police reached the protest site before that and detained some of them.

They were later released, the wife of one of the hostages confirmed to Dawn in the afternoon.

“They were taken to the police station and kept there for a long time, and the police were not allowing us to see them. The police misbehaved with us and told us to go away,” said Ayesha Ameen, whose husband, Ameen Bin Shams, was a fitter on the hijacked ship.

“They were arrested around 7:45am,” added Ayesha, who was not detained by police.

She said that the protesters were taken to the Tipu Sultan police station and alleged that 11 protesters were detained, including “underage individuals”.

A police official, who requested anonymity, also confirmed that the detained individuals had been released.

A senior police officer, who wished not to be named, denied that any protester was arrested. He said if there had been an arrest, it would have been mentioned in the police’s roznamcha (logbook).

Instead, the officer asserted that the police had engaged the protestors since Sunday night.

He said police officers had tried to persuade the families to vacate the place when they gathered at the Mofa office and asked them to hold their protest at a designated venue such as Karachi Press Club.

The officer told Dawn that the police dispersed the protesters without using any force. He also denied resorting to baton charges against the demonstrators.

Earlier, Ayesha recorded a video message at the protest site and said the families had been demanding the recovery of the hostages for four and a half months; however, “no one is listening to us”.

She added that the protesters were not blocking any roads or engaged in illegal activity but were merely protesting peacefully.

“We came here for the hostages’ release, not to become prisoners ourselves,” she added.

Another protester recorded a video inside a vehicle that appeared to be a police van. Police personnel could be seen standing outside the van in the video, in which Talib Raza, the maternal uncle of a second engineer on the ship, decried the detention of the protesters.

“We have been arrested — our women, elders and kids. It is shameful.

“Bilawal Bhutto sahib, we did not expect this from you,” Raza said, expressing disappointment.

In another video, a woman was also seen inside a vehicle that appeared to be a police van. Meanwhile, another woman could be heard saying, “Look, we are being arrested. This is our government, and this is our police. We are being taken away only because we spoke up for ourselves.”

In a video shared by Ayesha, two police officials could be seen manhandling an individual and forcing him into the police mobile.

Distress messages

Since the sailors’ hijacking, the crew has also made several emotional videos and audio appeals , while reporting that they have run out of clean water, food and medicine.

The last message from them came on August 7, more than 100 days after being taken hostage by Somali pirates. In that video, they appealed directly to the Pakistani government for their release.

They appeared to be in a state of extreme distress, with most looking sick and weak. The hostages requested that the Pakistani government talk to the Somali pirates and take steps to release them.

The hostages are victims of an “ ownership crisis ” because it is not clear who owns the ship, and the man previously thought to be the owner was later revealed to be more likely a middleman who hired them.

Last month, in a meeting with the International Maritime Organisation’s head, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar pressed for “urgent and effective institutional intervention” for the return of the Pakistani sailors.

Earlier that month, he had also directed “stakeholders” to intensify diplomatic engagement with national and international partners to facilitate the release.

The Foreign Office has also maintained that it remains “actively engaged” to secure the release of the seamen.

Additional reporting by Imtiaz Ali

World.title: Mir Raza murder case: Karachi police surgeon among 4 told to appear before judicial commission tomorrow
World.content:
KARACHI: A judicial commission on Monday summoned the Karachi police surgeon and another member included in the medical board that oversaw the exhumation of Mir Raza Ali’s body — which was found with a gunshot wound in July in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar — at the next hearing.

The murder case has been mired in conspiracy, with the 25-year-old victim’s family accusing police of trying to bury the facts and law enforcers initially trying to build the case around the possibility of suicide.

Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiyya Syed had previously also pointed out flaws in the findings of Ali’s first autopsy, following which his body was exhumed and a second post-mortem was conducted, whose findings ruled out the possibility of suicide.

A one-member judicial commission headed by Sindh High Court Justice Omar Sial, formed to investigate the circumstances and possible negligence in the case, has been holding hearings on the matter.

According to the commission’s order issued after today’s hearing, Ferozabad Station House Officer (SHO) Adeel Afzal and Gulistan-i-Jauhar police station Head Moharir Zeeshan have also been asked to appear before the commission at the next hearing on Sept 8.

SHO Afzal is deployed at the Ferozabad police station, where the case was initially registered under charges of kidnapping following Ali’s disappearance on July 28. His body was found a day later, and following Ali’s second autopsy, the probe was transferred to the Zaman Town police station in August, with murder charges added to the FIR.

Head Moharir Zeeshan is among those who visited the crime scene after Ali’s body was found.

In the order, Justice Sial stated that he had “realised during this hearing that the initial witnesses’ statements have not been provided to me. I have drawn an adverse inference from this”.

He recalled that on the first hearing held by the commission, the Sindh police was directed to provide the statements of all witnesses recorded under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

“However, this has not been done,” Justice Sial noted.

He added that a notice was issued to Sindh Deputy Inspector General (Crime and Investigation) Amir Farooqui — who also heads the new police team formed to probe the case — after which two statements from Ali’s friends, Abdul Razique and Muhammad Hasem, recorded on August 1, were provided by the Sindh Police.

“They say that there is no other document missing from the record after the submission of these two statements. The notice to DIG Amir Farooqui is therefore withdrawn on the assurance of the Home additional secretary that no further documents are missing,” the order read.

The additional secretary was also instructed to probe whether there were forensic, ballistic and chemical reports which had not been provided to the commission, and if there were any such reports, their copies should be submitted in a sealed envelope.

The case

Days after the recovery of Ali’s body on July 29, Dr Syed had told Geo News that the post-mortem findings in the case had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

On August 6, a Karachi court took up an application by Ali’s father, allowed the exhumation of his body, ordered the formation of a medico-legal board for the purpose and directed that a second autopsy of Ali’s body be conducted.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with police surgeon Dr Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed.

But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, the counsel for Ali’s family, Nasir, accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts.

The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on August 8.

A day later, the Sindh inspector general of police’s (IG) office notified the reconstitution of the investigating team probing Ali’s death while Karachi Additional IG Azad Khan transferred the investigation into Ali’s murder to Zaman Town police station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was registered.

The order for the probe team’s reconstitution also showed that a murder charge had been added to the first information report.

The same day, the Sindh government decided to seek a judicial commission for the case’s investigation, only to defer the plan a day later after Ali’s family said they had made no such demand and had faith in the new investigation team.

On Aug 19, Ali’s parents, Mir Hussain and Mariam Hussain, wrote to Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, seeking his “direct supervision of the murder investigation”. They also urged the chief minister to order an investigation and departmental inquiry into the previous investigation team and immediately suspend the officers involved.

The provincial government acknowledged the letter and announced the decision on Aug 23 to form a judicial commission to determine whether the investigation in the case was being conducted impartially and to investigate the circumstances surrounding Ali’s death.

However, soon after the announcement, the counsel for Ali’s family raised objections and later approached the Sindh High Court (SHC).

The petition was filed on August 24 in objection to the provincial government’s decision to form a judicial commission and sought the formation of an independent and multi-agency JIT “comprising officers who have had no previous involvement in the case” in place of the commission.

On Sept 2, the SHC dismissed a petition filed by Ali’s family, seeking the formation of a JIT to probe his murder, observing that constituting such a body was the “prerogative of the government”.

Meanwhile, the final report of Ali’s second post-mortem for the Mir Raza Ali murder case confirmed that his death was caused by a gunshot wound to the back.

“Death occurred due to cardiac rupture consequent to perforating firearm injury of the chest,” the report stated, adding that the entry wound was on the posterior thorax (back) and the exit wound on the anterior thorax (front of the chest).

“The findings are inconsistent with suicide as the manner of death,” it confirmed.

World.title: Pakistan at ‘very start’ of Test rebuilding process, says bowling coach Noffke
World.content:
Pakistan are at the “very start” of rebuilding their Test side, bowling coach Ashley Noffke said on Monday, as the team attempts to move past a tumultuous week that has seen sweeping changes to the squad and a shake-up of its coaching staff.

“Every nation has a life cycle, and there’ll be moments where they play really great cricket for long periods and then older players will move out and younger players will come in. And we’re at the very start of that process,” Noffke told reporters at Edgbaston.

The contrast with England, who are attempting to complete a 3-0 series sweep after emphatic victories at Headingley and Lord’s, could hardly be starker.

While Pakistan have brought in a new interim head coach in Mike Hesson, made wholesale changes to their squad and sent Noffke to England at short notice, the hosts have been able to build on a settled pace attack led by Jofra Archer, who says he is finally enjoying a period of stability after years of injury.

Pakistan’s changes have opened the door for young fast bowlers Razaullah and Mohammad Imran Jr, with Noffke viewing their presence in England as part of a longer-term plan rather than simply an emergency response to two defeats.

“They’re young guys. They haven’t experienced England conditions and they’re over here to learn and grow,” he said. “I think with any life cycle of any cricket team, you need to take a forward-thinking approach to what we might need in the future. I think other teams have been doing that and it’s now our turn to bring young guys over, make sure they get accustomed to conditions that are different to theirs at home.”

Both bowlers offer Pakistan something that has been missing from their attack during the series — pace. Noffke said they were “certainly closer to the 140 mark” than some of the quicks Pakistan had previously used.

Imran Jr, a left-armer, and Razaullah, a right-armer with a different action, could also provide variety to an attack that has relied heavily on veteran seamer Mohammad Abbas.

“Abbas has obviously bowled amazingly through this series and we need to support him as best we can,” Noffke said.

Noffke himself was thrust into the Test set-up at short notice, saying he received a message “at 3am” informing him that management was sending him to England.

Asked whether he had been given an explanation for the sweeping changes to the squad, he said: “Not really.”

“It’s not my job to be in consultation with where they see who’s in and who’s out. That’s obviously the selection panel,” he said.

“As we’ve already asked Mike [Hesson] in previous interviews, he’s only just come into that phase. So, like we said before, it’s unsettling, but it’s about getting on with it, focusing on what’s ahead of us as a Test-playing squad and trying to develop in all areas.”

The uncertainty surrounding Pakistan has also been compounded by an internal PCB disciplinary inquiry into the conduct of some players announced on Monday.

Noffke said he knew no more about the matter than the media did.

“As much as you do. And I can be really honest in that — I don’t know too much,” he said. “I sit outside of that decision-making model above us as coaches.”

He said the coaching staff had attempted to keep the players focused on the cricket rather than the developments surrounding them.

“There’s obviously a feeling of uncertainty, but they’ve just got back on the job,” Noffke said. “I’ve been really impressed with the level of calmness that they’ve taken over the last couple of days once we’ve given them time to talk.”

The Australian said Pakistan’s immediate strategy was straightforward: “good Test cricket”, discipline, bowling in good areas and building long partnerships with the bat.

Asked whether Pakistan risked becoming a laughing stock following the events on and off the field and whether the team needed to restore some pride, Noffke said performances were the only meaningful answer.

“Well, you only install pride with really good cricket, don’t you?” he said. “There’s no question that we need to develop our game. Our Test game needs to improve. But that doesn’t mean that we should be worried about that.”

England, meanwhile, are preparing for the possibility of completing a clean sweep with a fast-bowling unit that has been one of the defining features of the series.

Archer, who returned to Test cricket in July last year after more than four years away, believes he is now in a “good place” following a succession of career-threatening injuries.

The Barbados-born quick arrived in England in 2015 and four years later spearheaded the attack during England’s dramatic World Cup triumph at Lord’s, while also starring in the 2019 Ashes.

But an elbow problem subsequently developed, followed by back injuries, and Archer was sidelined from Test cricket from February 2021 until July 2025.

The 31-year-old, who continues to play all three international formats, said his long periods away from the game had also brought unexpected benefits.

“The time when I was injured, I really got away from cricket,” he told the BBC on Monday. “It’s all been a blur. I didn’t realise how long the time out was, either.”

Archer said the enforced breaks allowed him to spend more time at home in Barbados after moving to England.

“I got to spend some time at home, because, moving over, I never really got more than a couple of weeks,” he said. “To spend a month here and there, it was really nice.”

“I’d be lying if I didn’t say I had a good time away from everything. Now, everything is really nice. My body is in a good place, the team is in a good place and everyone is in a good place. I just want to play cricket.”

Archer has played a key role in England’s two victories over Pakistan and will be central to their bid for a 3-0 result at Edgbaston.

His presence has also added further weight to an England pace attack featuring Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson, with the group beginning to draw comparisons with England’s celebrated “Fab Four” of Matthew Hoggard, Steve Harmison, Simon Jones and Andrew Flintoff, who helped secure the 2005 Ashes.

Pakistan, by contrast, are still deciding whether to field four seamers or retain a spinner, with Noffke saying the decision would depend on the pitch and weather.

“We’ve got some really good options now to select in terms of the four seamers, our spinner that can bat. There are some great selection dilemmas, which is nice,” he said.

The Edgbaston pitch has plenty of grass, but Noffke expects it to be a good surface.

“It looks a good surface. There’s plenty of grass on it, though,” he said.

For Pakistan, however, the significance of Wednesday’s Test extends beyond avoiding a series whitewash.

With new faces being introduced amid considerable upheaval, Edgbaston could offer an early glimpse of the side Noffke believes is only now beginning the process of rebuilding.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures.
